description: Official NCERT Master Question Bank containing 2,633 real NCERT questions with exact page citations, verbatim quotes, official headings, and complete step-by-step solutions for NEET-UG candidates.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In a vernier callipers, 10 vernier scale divisions coincide with 9 main scale divisions. If each main scale division is 0.1 cm, the vernier constant is:

options.B: 0.1 cm

questions.explanation: Vernier constant = 1 MSD - 1 VSD = 1 MSD - (9/10) MSD = (1/10) MSD = 0.1 * 0.1 cm = 0.01 cm.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Vernier constant = 1 MSD - 1 VSD.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A screw gauge has a pitch of 0.5 mm and 50 circular scale divisions. The least count of the screw gauge is:

options.D: 0.1 mm

questions.explanation: Least Count = Pitch / Total circular scale divisions = 0.5 mm / 50 = 0.01 mm.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Least count of screw gauge = Pitch / Number of divisions on circular scale.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The dimensions of critical velocity vc of a liquid flowing through a tube are expressed as [η^x ρ^y r^z], where η is coefficient of viscosity, ρ is density of liquid, and r is radius of tube. The values of x, y and z respectively are:
questions.explanation: Reynolds number formula: vc = (R_e * η) / (ρ * r). Dimensions of η = [M L^-1 T^-1], ρ = [M L^-3], r = [L]. Equating powers gives x = 1, y = -1, z = -1.

ncert_reference.official_section: Section 1.7: Dimensional Analysis and its Applications
ncert_reference.exact_quote: Dimensional analysis can be used to deduce relations among physical quantities.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A body of mass m is thrown vertically upwards with speed u. It experiences constant air resistance force F resisting its motion. The ratio of time of ascent to time of descent is:

options.A: sqrt((g - F/m) / (g + F/m))
options.B: sqrt((g + F/m) / (g - F/m))
options.D: (g - F/m) / (g + F/m)

questions.explanation: During ascent, total downward acceleration a_up = g + F/m. During descent, acceleration a_down = g - F/m. Since distance is equal (h = 1/2 a t^2), t_ascent / t_descent = sqrt(a_down / a_up) = sqrt((g - F/m) / (g + F/m)).

ncert_reference.exact_quote: When a resistive force acts opposing motion, deceleration during upward flight is greater than acceleration during downward fall.

questions.question: A car accelerates from rest at a constant rate α for some time, after which it decelerates at a constant rate β to come to rest. If total time elapsed is t, the maximum velocity attained is:

options.B: vmax = (α + β) * t / (α * β)
options.C: vmax = sqrt(α * β) * t
options.D: vmax = (α * t) / β

questions.explanation: t = t1 + t2 = vmax/α + vmax/β = vmax * (α + β) / (α * β) => vmax = (α * β * t) / (α + β).

ncert_reference.official_section: Section 2.5: Kinematic Equations for Uniformly Accelerated Motion

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A particle moves in a circle of radius 5 cm with constant speed and time period 0.2 π seconds. The acceleration of the particle is:
questions.explanation: ω = 2π / T = 2π / (0.2 π) = 10 rad/s. Centripetal acceleration a = ω^2 * r = 10^2 * (0.05 m) = 100 * 0.05 = 5 m/s^2.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Centripetal acceleration magnitude is ac = ω^2 r = v^2 / r.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A projectile is thrown with speed u at an angle θ with the horizontal. The radius of curvature of its trajectory at the highest point is:

options.A: u^2 * cos^2(θ) / g
options.B: u^2 / g
options.C: u^2 * sin^2(θ) / g
options.D: u^2 * cos(θ) / g

questions.explanation: At the highest point, speed is purely horizontal (v = u cos θ) and normal acceleration is g. Radius of curvature R = v^2 / an = (u cos θ)^2 / g = u^2 cos^2(θ) / g.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: At the peak of projectile motion, the vertical component of velocity is zero.

questions.question: A thin uniform rod of length L and mass M is free to rotate in a vertical plane about a horizontal axis through one of its ends. If it is released from the horizontal position, the angular acceleration of the rod at the instant of release is:

options.B: g / L

questions.explanation: Torque about pivot: τ = M * g * (L/2). Moment of inertia about end: I = (1/3) M L^2. Angular acceleration α = τ / I = (M g L / 2) / (M L^2 / 3) = 3g / (2L).

ncert_reference.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
ncert_reference.exact_quote: Torque is τ = I α.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The ratio of escape velocity from earth's surface to orbital velocity of a satellite orbiting very close to earth's surface is:

options.A: sqrt(2) : 1
options.B: 1 : sqrt(2)

questions.explanation: Escape velocity ve = sqrt(2 g R). Orbital velocity near surface vo = sqrt(g R). Ratio ve / vo = sqrt(2) / 1.

ncert_reference.official_section: Section 7.6: Escape Speed and Orbital Speed
ncert_reference.exact_quote: ve = √2 vo; escape speed from surface is √2 times the orbital speed near earth.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The escape velocity from the surface of Earth is ve = 11.2 km/s. If a planet has twice the radius of Earth and four times its mass, the escape velocity from the planet's surface is:

options.D: 5.6 km/s

questions.explanation: ve = sqrt(2GM / R). For the new planet: ve' = sqrt(2G(4M) / (2R)) = sqrt(2) * ve = 11.2 * 1.414 ≈ 15.84 km/s.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: The escape speed from the surface of Earth is ve = √(2GM/RE).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A satellite orbits Earth at altitude h = R (Earth radius). The orbital velocity of the satellite is:

options.A: sqrt(g R / 2)
options.B: sqrt(g R)
options.C: sqrt(2 g R)
options.D: g R / 2

questions.explanation: v0 = sqrt(GM / r) = sqrt(GM / (R + h)). With h = R, r = 2R. Since GM = g R^2: v0 = sqrt(g R^2 / 2R) = sqrt(g R / 2).

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Orbital speed is v0 = √(GM / (RE + h)).

questions.question: A wire of natural length L and cross-sectional area A is stretched by a force F, producing elongation ΔL. The elastic potential energy stored per unit volume of the wire is:

options.B: Stress * Strain
options.C: (1/2) * Stress / Strain
options.D: Strain / (2 * Stress)

questions.explanation: Energy density u = U / Volume = (1/2) * (F * ΔL) / (A * L) = (1/2) * Stress * Strain.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Elastic energy density = (1/2) x stress x strain.

ncert_reference.official_section: Section 9.3: Pascal's Law and Hydraulic Machines

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The work done in blowing a soap bubble of radius R is W. The additional work done in expanding it from radius R to radius 2R is (surface tension T):

options.A: 3 W
options.B: 4 W
options.C: 2 W
options.D: W

questions.explanation: A soap bubble has two surfaces. W1 = 2 * T * (4π R^2) = 8π T R^2. When expanded to 2R: W_total = 8π T (2R)^2 = 4 * (8π T R^2) = 4 W. Additional work = W_total - W1 = 4 W - W = 3 W.

ncert_reference.official_section: Section 9.6: Surface Tension and Surface Energy
ncert_reference.exact_quote: A soap bubble has two liquid-gas interfaces; hence work done is 2 x T x ΔA.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: According to Bernoulli's principle, for a streamline flow of an incompressible non-viscous fluid, along a streamline:

options.A: p + (1/2) ρ v^2 + ρ g h = Constant
options.B: p + ρ v^2 + ρ g h = Constant
options.C: p / ρ + v^2 + g h = Constant
options.D: p + (1/2) ρ v + ρ g h^2 = Constant

questions.explanation: Bernoulli's theorem states: p + (1/2)ρv^2 + ρgh = constant along a streamline for an ideal fluid.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Bernoulli's equation states that the sum of pressure, kinetic energy per unit volume, and potential energy per unit volume remains constant.

options.C: T / R
options.D: 8T / R

questions.explanation: A soap bubble has two liquid-gas interfaces (inner and outer). Thus ΔP = 2 * (2T / R) = 4T / R. For a liquid drop, ΔP = 2T / R.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: A soap bubble has two surfaces. The excess pressure is ΔP = 4S/r.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The terminal velocity vT of a small spherical ball of radius r falling through a viscous fluid of viscosity η is proportional to:

options.A: r^2 / η
options.B: r / η
options.C: r^2 * η
options.D: r / η^2

questions.explanation: By Stokes' Law: vT = [2 * r^2 * (ρ - σ) * g] / [9 * η]. Thus vT ∝ r^2 / η.

ncert_reference.official_section: Section 9.5: Stokes' Law and Terminal Velocity
ncert_reference.exact_quote: Terminal velocity is vT = (2/9) r^2 (ρ - σ) g / η.

questions.explanation: Equivalent resistance Req = R1 + R2 => 2L / (Keq * A) = L / (K1 * A) + L / (K2 * A) => 2 / Keq = 1/K1 + 1/K2 => Keq = 2 K1 K2 / (K1 + K2).

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Thermal resistance is R = L / (KA). For series combination, R = R1 + R2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In an adiabatic expansion of an ideal gas, the relation between temperature T and volume V is given by:

options.A: T * V^(γ - 1) = Constant
options.B: T * V^γ = Constant
options.C: T^(γ - 1) * V = Constant
options.D: T / V^(γ - 1) = Constant

questions.explanation: For an adiabatic process, P*V^γ = constant. Since P = nRT/V, substituting gives T * V^(γ - 1) = constant.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: For an adiabatic process of an ideal gas, TV^(γ-1) = constant.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A simple pendulum of length L has period T. If it is placed inside an elevator accelerating downwards with acceleration a = g/2, the new period is:

options.A: sqrt(2) T
options.B: T / sqrt(2)
options.C: 2 T

questions.explanation: Effective g_eff = g - a = g - g/2 = g/2. T' = 2π sqrt(L / g_eff) = 2π sqrt(L / (g/2)) = sqrt(2) * 2π sqrt(L/g) = sqrt(2) T.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: T = 2π √(L / g_eff).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A simple pendulum executes SHM with time period T. If its length is increased by 21%, the percentage increase in its time period is:
questions.explanation: T = 2π * sqrt(L / g). T' / T = sqrt(1.21 L / L) = 1.10. Percentage increase = (1.10 - 1) * 100% = 10%.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: The period of a simple pendulum is T = 2π√(L/g).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The speed of sound in hydrogen gas at STP compared to that in oxygen gas at STP is:

options.A: 4 times
options.B: 16 times
options.C: 2 times
options.D: 1/4 times

questions.explanation: Speed v = sqrt(γ R T / M). Since both H2 and O2 are diatomic (same γ): v(H2) / v(O2) = sqrt(M(O2) / M(H2)) = sqrt(32 / 2) = sqrt(16) = 4.

ncert_reference.official_section: Section 14.4: Speed of a Longitudinal Wave
ncert_reference.exact_quote: Speed of sound in an ideal gas depends inversely on square root of molecular mass: v = √(γRT / M).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In an organ pipe open at both ends, the fundamental frequency is f0. The frequency of its third harmonic is:
questions.explanation: An open organ pipe produces all harmonics: f_n = n * f0 (n = 1, 2, 3...). The third harmonic corresponds to n = 3, so frequency is 3 f0.

ncert_reference.official_section: Section 14.8: Standing Waves and Normal Modes
ncert_reference.exact_quote: For an open pipe, frequencies are integer multiples of the fundamental: fn = n v / (2L).

questions.question: An electric dipole of dipole moment p is aligned at 30° with a uniform electric field E. The torque experienced by the dipole is:

options.A: p E / 2
options.B: p E
options.C: sqrt(3) p E / 2
options.D: Zero

questions.explanation: Torque τ = p * E * sin(θ) = p * E * sin(30°) = p * E * 0.5 = p E / 2.

ncert_reference.official_section: Section 1.11: Dipole in a Uniform External Field
ncert_reference.exact_quote: The magnitude of torque on a dipole in a uniform electric field is τ = p E sin θ.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two point charges +4q and +q are placed separated by distance r. A third charge Q is placed on the line joining them such that all three charges are in equilibrium. The magnitude, sign, and position of Q are:

options.A: -4q/9, at distance 2r/3 from +4q
options.B: +4q/9, at distance r/3 from +4q
options.C: -q/4, at midpoint
options.D: -2q/3, at distance r/2 from +q

questions.explanation: For net force on Q to be 0: k (4q) Q / x^2 = k q Q / (r-x)^2 => 2/(x) = 1/(r-x) => x = 2r/3 from +4q. For +q to be in equilibrium: k (4q)(q) / r^2 + k Q q / (r/3)^2 = 0 => Q = -4q/9.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Principle of superposition states that net electric force on any charge is the vector sum of individual forces.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two point charges +3 μC and +8 μC repel each other with a force of 40 N. If a charge of -5 μC is added to each of them, then the force between them will become:

options.A: 10 N (Attractive)
options.B: 20 N (Repulsive)
options.C: 10 N (Repulsive)
options.D: 5 N (Attractive)

questions.explanation: Initial charges q1 = +3, q2 = +8 => q1*q2 = 24. F1 = 40 N. New charges q1' = 3 - 5 = -2 μC, q2' = 8 - 5 = +3 μC => q1'*q2' = -6. F2 / F1 = |q1'*q2'| / (q1*q2) = 6 / 24 = 1/4. F2 = 40 / 4 = 10 N, and since signs are opposite, the force is attractive.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Coulomb force is directly proportional to product of magnitudes of charges and attractive between opposite charges.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two point charges +4q and +q are placed at a distance L apart. A third charge Q is placed at a distance x from +4q on the line joining them. For Q to be in electrostatic equilibrium, x must be:
questions.explanation: For net force on Q to be zero: k*(4q)*Q / x^2 = k*q*Q / (L - x)^2 => 2 / x = 1 / (L - x) => 2L - 2x = x => 3x = 2L => x = 2L / 3.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Coulomb's force between two charges is directly proportional to product of charges and inversely proportional to square of distance.

options.D: Dependent on surface area

questions.explanation: By Gauss's Law: Φ = q_enclosed / ε0. If q_enclosed = 0, the net electric flux is zero.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Gauss's law states that total electric flux through a closed surface is equal to q_enclosed / ε0.

questions.question: If a parallel plate capacitor with air between the plates is charged to potential V and then disconnected from battery, what happens when a dielectric slab of constant K is inserted?

options.A: Charge remains constant, potential decreases to V/K
options.B: Charge increases K times, potential remains constant
options.C: Capacitance decreases to C/K
options.D: Energy stored increases K times

questions.explanation: Since battery is disconnected, charge Q remains conserved. Capacitance increases to C' = K*C. Potential difference decreases to V' = Q / C' = V / K.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: When battery is disconnected and dielectric is inserted, charge remains constant and potential difference decreases by factor K.

questions.question: Two capacitors of capacitances 2 μF and 6 μF are connected in series across 120 V. The charge on the 2 μF capacitor is:

options.A: 180 μC
options.B: 240 μC
options.C: 120 μC
options.D: 360 μC

questions.explanation: Equivalent capacitance Ceq = (2 * 6) / (2 + 6) = 12 / 8 = 1.5 μF. Total charge Q = Ceq * V = 1.5 * 120 = 180 μC. In series, charge on both capacitors is identical.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: In a series combination, the charge Q on each capacitor is the same.

questions.question: The drift velocity (vd) of conduction electrons in a metallic conductor is related to the applied electric field (E) and relaxation time (τ) by the relation:

options.A: vd = - (e * E * τ) / m
options.B: vd = - (m * E * τ) / e
options.C: vd = - (e * m * E) / τ
options.D: vd = - (e * τ) / (m * E)

questions.explanation: According to NCERT Physics, acceleration is a = -eE/m. The average drift velocity acquired over relaxation time τ is vd = a * τ = -(eEτ)/m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: If the radius of a cylindrical metallic wire is stretched uniformly to half its original value while keeping the volume constant, its resistance becomes:

options.A: 16 times original resistance
options.B: 4 times original resistance
options.C: 8 times original resistance
options.D: 1/16 times original resistance

questions.explanation: Volume V = A * L is constant. If radius r' = r/2, area A' = A/4, which means length L' = 4L. Since R = ρL/A, R' = ρ(4L)/(A/4) = 16(ρL/A) = 16R.

options.D: j = σ * E^2

questions.question: Magnetic flux linked with a coil of resistance 10 Ω changes according to Φ = 6t^2 - 5t + 1. The induced current at t = 0.25 s is:

options.B: 2 A
options.D: 4 A

questions.explanation: Induced EMF e = -dΦ/dt = -(12t - 5). At t = 0.25 s: e = -(12 * 0.25 - 5) = -(3 - 5) = 2 V. Induced current I = e / R = 2 / 10 = 0.2 A.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Induced emf is e = -dΦB/dt and I = e / R.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An alternating voltage V = 200 * sqrt(2) * sin(100 t) V is connected to a 1 μF capacitor through an AC ammeter. The reading of the ammeter is:

options.A: 20 mA
options.B: 40 mA
options.C: 10 mA
options.D: 100 mA

questions.explanation: Vrms = 200 V. Capacitive reactance XC = 1 / (ω C) = 1 / (100 * 10^-6) = 10,000 Ω. Irms = Vrms / XC = 200 / 10,000 = 0.02 A = 20 mA.

ncert_reference.official_section: Section 7.4: AC Voltage Applied to a Capacitor
ncert_reference.exact_quote: Capacitive reactance is XC = 1 / (ω C) and Irms = Vrms / XC.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In a series LCR circuit at resonance, which of the following conditions is TRUE?

options.A: Impedance Z is minimum (Z = R) and current amplitude is maximum
options.B: Inductive reactance XL is zero
options.C: Current is out of phase with applied voltage by π/2
options.D: Impedance Z is infinite

questions.explanation: At electrical resonance in series LCR: XL = XC, impedance Z = sqrt(R^2 + (XL - XC)^2) = R (minimum), power factor cos φ = 1, and current is maximum and in phase with voltage.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: At resonance, Z = R and the current amplitude is maximum: Im = Vm / R.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The power transmitted by an AC circuit is zero if the phase difference φ between current and voltage is:

options.C: π

questions.explanation: P = Vrms * Irms * cos(φ). When φ = π/2 (purely inductive or capacitive circuit), cos(π/2) = 0, giving zero power (wattless current).

ncert_reference.exact_quote: If φ = π/2, power is zero. The current in this case is called wattless current.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which electromagnetic radiation has the highest frequency in the electromagnetic spectrum?

options.A: Gamma rays
options.B: X-rays
options.C: Ultraviolet rays
options.D: Microwaves

questions.explanation: Gamma rays have the shortest wavelength (< 10^-12 m) and correspondingly highest frequency (> 10^20 Hz) in the EM spectrum.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Gamma rays lie in the upper frequency range of electromagnetic spectrum and have wavelengths from about 10^-10 m to less than 10^-14 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Displacement current ID across the plates of a charging capacitor is given by Maxwell's formula:

options.A: ID = ε0 * (dΦE / dt)
options.B: ID = μ0 * (dΦE / dt)
options.C: ID = ε0 * (dΦB / dt)
options.D: ID = (1 / ε0) * (dΦE / dt)

questions.explanation: Maxwell introduced displacement current ID = ε0 * (dΦE / dt) to resolve Ampere's circuital law inconsistency.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Equation (8.4): id = ε0 dΦE/dt is called displacement current.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In an electromagnetic wave traveling along the +x direction, if the electric field oscillates along the +y direction, the magnetic field must oscillate along the:

options.A: +z direction
options.B: -y direction
options.C: +x direction
options.D: -z direction

questions.explanation: Poynting vector S = (1/μ0) * (E x B) points in direction of wave propagation (+x). Since E is along +y (j^) and (j^ x k^ = i^), B must be along +z (k^).

ncert_reference.exact_quote: The direction of propagation of EM waves is given by the vector cross product E x B.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In an electromagnetic wave in free space, the root mean square value of the electric field is Erms = 6 V/m. The peak value of the magnetic field B0 is:
questions.explanation: Peak electric field E0 = sqrt(2) * Erms = 1.414 * 6 = 8.485 V/m. Speed of light c = E0 / B0, so B0 = E0 / c = 8.485 / (3 * 10^8) ≈ 2.83 * 10^-8 T.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: The amplitudes of electric and magnetic fields in free space are related by c = E0 / B0.

questions.question: A convex mirror of focal length f produces an image of a real object that is always:

options.A: Virtual, erect, and diminished between pole and focus
options.B: Real, inverted, and magnified
options.C: Real, inverted, and diminished
options.D: Virtual, inverted, and of the same size

questions.explanation: For any real object placed in front of a convex mirror, the image formed is always virtual, erect, and diminished, located between the pole and the principal focus.

ncert_reference.official_section: Section 9.2: Reflection of Light by Spherical Mirrors
ncert_reference.exact_quote: A convex mirror always gives a virtual, erect, and diminished image of an object placed anywhere in front of it.

questions.question: A light ray travels from a denser medium of refractive index n1 into a rarer medium of refractive index n2. The critical angle for total internal reflection ic is given by:

options.A: sin(ic) = n2 / n1
options.B: sin(ic) = n1 / n2
options.C: cos(ic) = n2 / n1
options.D: tan(ic) = n1 / n2

questions.explanation: By Snell's law: n1 * sin(ic) = n2 * sin(90°). Since sin(90°) = 1, sin(ic) = n2 / n1.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: sin ic = n2 / n1. If the rarer medium is air, sin ic = 1 / n.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Optical fibres transmit optical signals across long distances with minimal loss based on the phenomenon of:

options.A: Total internal reflection at the core-cladding boundary
options.B: Diffraction of light waves
options.C: Polarisation of transverse waves
options.D: Scattering of light by colloidal particles

questions.explanation: Optical fibres consist of a core with higher refractive index surrounded by cladding of lower refractive index. Light guided through the core undergoes successive total internal reflections.

ncert_reference.official_section: Section 9.4.1: Total Internal Reflection in Nature and Technology (Optical Fibres)
ncert_reference.exact_quote: Optical fibres are fabricated with high quality composite glass/quartz fibres... light undergoes repeated total internal reflections along the length of the fibre.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A glass prism has a refracting angle A = 60° and its refractive index is n = sqrt(3). What is the angle of minimum deviation Dm produced by the prism?
questions.explanation: At minimum deviation: n = sin((A + Dm)/2) / sin(A/2). Here sin(A/2) = sin(30°) = 1/2. Thus sin((60° + Dm)/2) = sqrt(3) * (1/2) = sqrt(3)/2, so (60° + Dm)/2 = 60° => Dm = 60°.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: n21 = sin[(A + Dm)/2] / sin(A/2) is the prism formula.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: According to the Lens Maker's formula, the focal length f of a thin lens with radii of curvature R1 and R2 and relative refractive index n is given by:
questions.explanation: The Lens Maker's formula is 1/f = (n - 1) * [1/R1 - 1/R2].

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Equation (9.22): 1/f = (n2/n1 - 1) (1/R1 - 1/R2). This is known as the lens maker's formula.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An equiconvex lens of focal length f made of glass (n = 1.5) is immersed in water (n = 1.33). What will happen to its focal length in water?

options.A: It increases to roughly 4 times its focal length in air
options.B: It decreases to 1/4th of its value in air
options.C: It remains unchanged
options.D: It becomes negative (diverging)

ncert_reference.exact_quote: When a lens is immersed in a liquid of refractive index less than the lens material, its focal length increases substantially.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two thin lenses of focal lengths +20 cm and -40 cm are placed in coaxial contact. What is the power of the combination in dioptres?

ncert_reference.official_section: Section 9.5.3: Power of a Lens & Combination of Thin Lenses in Contact
ncert_reference.exact_quote: The total power of the combination is P = P1 + P2 + ... where P is in dioptres when f is in metres.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In a compound microscope, the focal length of the objective lens (fo) and eyepiece lens (fe) satisfy which condition for high magnification?

options.A: Both fo and fe are short, with fo < fe
options.B: fo is very large and fe is very small
options.C: Both fo and fe are extremely large
options.D: fo > fe and both are negative

questions.explanation: In a compound microscope, both objective and eyepiece lenses have short focal lengths to achieve high magnification, with the objective having a shorter focal length than the eyepiece (fo < fe).

ncert_reference.exact_quote: The objective has a smaller focal length and aperture than the eyepiece; both lenses have short focal lengths.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In an astronomical telescope in normal adjustment (image at infinity), the magnifying power m and tube length L are given respectively by:

options.A: m = fo / fe and L = fo + fe
options.B: m = fe / fo and L = fo - fe
options.C: m = (fo * fe) / L and L = fo + fe
options.D: m = fo / fe and L = fo * fe

questions.explanation: In normal adjustment of an astronomical telescope: magnifying power m = fo / fe, and the distance between objective and eyepiece is L = fo + fe.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: The magnifying power is m = fo / fe and length of the telescope tube is L = fo + fe.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Why do reflecting telescopes (such as the Cassegrain telescope) possess a major advantage over refracting telescopes?

options.A: Mirrors are free from chromatic aberration and can be supported easily over the entire back surface to avoid spherical aberration
options.B: Mirrors produce higher dispersion of visible light
options.C: Mirrors do not reflect light according to the law of reflection
options.D: Mirrors cannot form real images

questions.explanation: Reflecting telescopes have no chromatic aberration (since reflection does not depend on wavelength) and parabolic mirrors eliminate spherical aberration while providing superior mechanical support.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: There is no chromatic aberration in a mirror. If a parabolic reflecting surface is chosen, spherical aberration is also removed.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Blue colour of the sky is explained by Rayleigh scattering. According to Rayleigh's law, the intensity of scattered light I is proportional to:
questions.explanation: Rayleigh scattering law states that the amount of scattering is inversely proportional to the fourth power of the wavelength: I ∝ 1 / λ^4.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: The amount of scattering is inversely proportional to the fourth power of the wavelength: I ∝ 1/λ^4 (Rayleigh scattering).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In a primary rainbow, what sequence of internal reflection and refractions occurs inside a spherical raindrop?

options.A: Two refractions and one internal reflection
options.B: Two refractions and two internal reflections
options.C: One refraction and one reflection
options.D: Three internal reflections only

questions.explanation: A primary rainbow is formed by sunlight undergoing two refractions (entering and exiting the drop) and one internal reflection inside the water drop.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: The primary rainbow is a result of three-step process, that is, refraction with dispersion, followed by an internal reflection and finally refraction again.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A secondary rainbow is fainter than a primary rainbow because:

options.A: It involves two internal reflections inside the raindrops, losing more light at each reflection
options.B: It is formed by infrared radiation
options.C: It is formed by light reflected from the earth's surface
options.D: It has red on the inside and violet on the outside

questions.explanation: A secondary rainbow is formed by four-step process: two refractions and two internal reflections. Light is lost at each reflection, making it fainter than the primary rainbow.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: It is due to four-step process. Such a rainbow is called secondary rainbow... It is fainter than the primary rainbow.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A person with myopia (near-sightedness) cannot clearly see objects beyond a certain far point. Which lens is used to correct myopia?

options.A: Concave lens of appropriate focal length
options.B: Convex lens of appropriate focal length
options.C: Bifocal cylindrical lens
options.D: Plano-convex lens

questions.explanation: In myopia, light rays from a distant object focus in front of the retina. A concave (diverging) lens is used to diverge the rays so that they focus on the retina.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: A concave lens is interposed between the eye and the object to form a virtual image at the far point of the myopic eye.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Hypermetropia (far-sightedness) is corrected using which type of lens?

options.A: Convex lens
options.B: Concave lens
options.C: Cylindrical lens
options.D: Diverging meniscus lens

questions.explanation: In hypermetropia, light rays from a nearby object focus behind the retina. A convex (converging) lens converges the incoming rays to focus sharply on the retina.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: A convergent lens is used to correct hypermetropia by providing additional converging power.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Astigmatism arises when the cornea is not spherical in shape (having different curvatures in different planes). It is corrected using:

options.A: Cylindrical lenses
options.B: Spherical concave lenses
options.C: Spherical convex lenses
options.D: Bifocal lenses

questions.explanation: Astigmatism occurs when the cornea is not spherical. This defect can be corrected using cylindrical glasses of desired radius of curvature.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Astigmatism can be corrected by using a cylindrical lens of desired radius of curvature with an appropriately directed axis.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A ray of light is incident at an angle of 60° on one face of an equilateral prism. If the angle of emergence is also 60°, what is the angle of deviation?
questions.explanation: Relation for prism: i + e = A + δ. Here i = 60°, e = 60°, and equilateral prism angle A = 60°. Therefore δ = i + e - A = 60° + 60° - 60° = 60°.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Equation (9.32): i + e = A + δ.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Mirage is an optical illusion observed in deserts during hot summer days caused by:

options.A: Total internal reflection of light rays passing through layers of air with decreasing refractive index near the hot ground
options.B: Scattering of sunlight by sand particles
options.C: Diffraction of light by air molecules
options.D: Interference of light waves

questions.explanation: Near the hot ground, air is warmer and less dense (lower refractive index). A ray from a tall tree travels from denser to rarer air, bending successively until the angle of incidence exceeds critical angle, undergoing total internal reflection.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: This optical illusion is called mirage. It is a consequence of total internal reflection.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A convex lens of focal length f1 is placed in contact with a concave lens of focal length f2. If f1 < f2, the combination behaves as a:

options.A: Converging lens (Convex lens)
options.B: Diverging lens (Concave lens)
options.C: Plane glass slab
options.D: Opaque surface

questions.explanation: Power P = 1/f1 - 1/f2. Since f1 < f2, 1/f1 > 1/f2, so net power P is positive (converging behavior).

ncert_reference.exact_quote: The nature of the combination is determined by the lens having the shorter focal length (greater power).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The power of accommodation of a normal human eye allows clear vision from a near point D of approximately:

options.A: 25 cm to infinity
options.B: 10 cm to 100 cm
options.C: 50 cm to infinity
options.D: 1 metre to infinity

questions.explanation: For a normal adult eye, the near point (least distance of distinct vision) is approximately 25 cm, and the far point is at infinity.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: The closest distance for which the lens can focus light on the retina is called the least distance of distinct vision, or the near point. For a normal adult eye, this is about 25 cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: When white light passes through a glass prism, which colour suffers the MAXIMUM deviation and why?

options.A: Violet, because refractive index of glass is maximum for violet (shortest wavelength in visible spectrum)
options.B: Red, because it has longest wavelength
options.C: Green, because it is the mean colour
options.D: Yellow, because it has highest speed in glass

questions.explanation: By Cauchy's dispersion formula, n decreases with increasing wavelength (n_violet > n_red). Since deviation δ ≈ (n - 1)A for thin prisms, violet light deviates the most.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Violet light bends the most, being not as fast as red light in glass, and red the least.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An object is placed at a distance of 15 cm from a concave mirror of focal length 10 cm. The magnification produced by the mirror is:

options.A: -2 (real, inverted and magnified)
options.B: +2 (virtual, erect)
options.C: -0.5 (diminished)
options.D: -1 (same size)

questions.explanation: Using mirror formula: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f. Here u = -15 cm, f = -10 cm. 1/v = -1/10 - (-1/15) = -1/30 => v = -30 cm. Magnification m = -v/u = -(-30)/(-15) = -2.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Linear magnification m = -v / u.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following phenomena proves the TRANSVERSE nature of light waves rather than longitudinal nature?

options.A: Polarisation
options.B: Refraction
options.C: Interference
options.D: Diffraction

questions.explanation: Polarisation can only occur in transverse waves where oscillations are perpendicular to the direction of propagation. Longitudinal waves cannot be polarised.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Polarisation demonstrates conclusively that light waves are transverse in character.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A convex lens of glass (n = 1.5) is immersed in carbon disulphide (n = 1.63). How does the lens behave in this medium?

options.A: It behaves as a diverging lens
options.B: It behaves as a converging lens with smaller focal length
options.C: It becomes completely opaque
options.D: It behaves as a plane mirror

questions.explanation: When surrounding medium has refractive index greater than the lens material (n_med > n_lens), the factor (n_lens/n_med - 1) becomes negative, reversing the optical character from converging to diverging.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: If a lens is placed in a medium of refractive index higher than its own, its focal length changes sign and its nature is reversed.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The apparent depth of a swimming pool filled with water of refractive index 4/3 having real depth 4 m as viewed normally from air is:

options.A: 3 m
options.C: 2 m

questions.explanation: Apparent depth = Real depth / n = 4 m / (4/3) = 3 m.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: The bottom of a tank filled with water appears raised due to refraction. Apparent depth = Real depth / n.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: At sunset and sunrise, the sun appears reddish because:

options.A: Red light has the longest wavelength and is least scattered by atmospheric molecules over the longer path length
options.B: The sun actually cools down at sunset
options.C: Red light travels faster in air than other colours
options.D: Atmosphere absorbs all red light

questions.explanation: Sunlight travels through a thicker layer of atmosphere at sunset and sunrise. Blue and shorter wavelengths are scattered away, leaving mostly red and orange rays to reach our eyes.

ncert_reference.official_section: Section 9.8.1: Blue of the Sky and Reddish Appearance of the Sun
ncert_reference.exact_quote: Light has to pass through a larger thickness of the atmosphere at sunrise and sunset... longer wavelengths are less scattered and reach the observer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The magnifying power of a simple microscope (magnifying glass) having focal length f when image is formed at near point D is:

options.A: m = 1 + D / f
options.B: m = D / f
options.C: m = 1 - D / f
options.D: m = f / D

questions.explanation: For image formed at the near point D: m = 1 + D/f. For image at infinity: m = D/f.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: When the image is formed at the near point, linear magnification is m = 1 + D / f.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In a Cassegrain reflecting telescope, the secondary mirror used is a:

options.A: Convex mirror
options.B: Concave mirror
options.C: Plane mirror only
options.D: Cylindrical lens

questions.explanation: In a Cassegrain telescope, light reflected from the primary concave parabolic mirror is focused toward a secondary convex mirror before passing through a central hole in the primary mirror to the eyepiece.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Figure 9.33: Cassegrain telescope uses a concave primary mirror and a convex secondary mirror.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The radius of curvature of each face of a biconvex lens made of glass (n = 1.5) is 20 cm. What is the focal length of the lens in air?

options.A: 20 cm
options.B: 10 cm
options.C: 40 cm
options.D: 15 cm

ncert_reference.exact_quote: For an equiconvex lens with n = 1.5, f = R.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Why are clouds generally white in colour?

options.A: Because cloud droplets (size 'a' >> λ) scatter all wavelengths of visible light nearly equally
options.B: Because clouds only contain gaseous oxygen
options.C: Because water drops absorb all red light
options.D: Because Rayleigh scattering condition is strictly satisfied

questions.explanation: When particle size 'a' is much larger than wavelength of light (a >> λ), Rayleigh's 1/λ^4 law does not apply. All colours are scattered equally, so clouds appear white.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: For large particles like water droplets and dust (a >> λ), scattering is nearly independent of wavelength and all colours are scattered equally. Hence clouds appear white.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A convex lens of focal length 20 cm is placed in contact with a concave lens of focal length 40 cm. The power of the combination is:

ncert_reference.official_section: Section 9.5.3: Combination of Thin Lenses in Contact
ncert_reference.exact_quote: The total power of thin lenses in contact is P = P1 + P2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In an astronomical telescope in normal adjustment, the focal length of objective is 100 cm and that of eyepiece is 5 cm. The magnifying power and tube length are:

options.A: 20 and 105 cm
options.B: 20 and 95 cm
options.C: 500 and 105 cm
options.D: 25 and 105 cm

questions.explanation: Magnifying power m = fo / fe = 100 / 5 = 20. Length of tube L = fo + fe = 100 + 5 = 105 cm.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: The magnifying power of an astronomical telescope in normal adjustment is m = fo / fe and tube length is fo + fe.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: For a prism of refracting angle A = 60°, if angle of minimum deviation Dm = 30°, the refractive index of the prism material is:

options.A: sqrt(2)
options.C: sqrt(3)

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Refractive index of prism is n = sin((A + Dm)/2) / sin(A/2).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A convex lens of focal length 20 cm is cut along the diameter into two equal plano-convex halves. The focal length of each half is:

options.A: 40 cm
options.B: 20 cm
options.C: 10 cm
options.D: 80 cm

questions.explanation: For original equiconvex lens: 1/f = (n - 1)(2/R) = 1/20. For each half: 1/f' = (n - 1)(1/R) = (1/2) * (1/f) = 1/40 => f' = 40 cm.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: When a lens is cut perpendicular to principal axis, focal length of each half doubles.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In Young's double slit experiment, if the separation between the slits is halved and distance of screen from slits is doubled, fringe width becomes:

options.A: 4 times
options.B: 2 times
options.C: Halved
options.D: Unchanged

questions.explanation: Fringe width β = λ D / d. When d' = d/2 and D' = 2D, β' = λ (2D) / (d/2) = 4 (λ D / d) = 4 β.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Fringe width β is given by β = λ D / d.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In Young's double slit experiment, if the separation between the slits is halved and the distance between the screen and slits is doubled, the fringe width becomes:

options.A: 4 times
options.B: 2 times
options.C: Halved
options.D: Unchanged

questions.explanation: Fringe width β = λ * D / d. If d' = d/2 and D' = 2D, β' = λ * (2D) / (d/2) = 4 * (λ D / d) = 4β.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: The fringe width is given by β = λ D / d.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A ray of light enters a glass slab of refractive index 1.5 at Brewster's angle. The angle between the reflected ray and refracted ray is:
questions.explanation: At Brewster's angle of incidence, the reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular to each other (angle = 90°).

ncert_reference.exact_quote: When light is incident at Brewster's angle, the reflected and refracted rays are mutually perpendicular.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two coherent sources of light have intensities I and 4I. The ratio of maximum to minimum intensity in their interference pattern is:
questions.explanation: Imax = (sqrt(4I) + sqrt(I))^2 = (2 + 1)^2 * I = 9I. Imin = (sqrt(4I) - sqrt(I))^2 = (2 - 1)^2 * I = 1I. Ratio = 9 : 1.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Imax = (√I1 + √I2)^2 and Imin = (√I1 - √I2)^2.

questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.question: The de Broglie wavelength of an electron accelerated through a potential difference of V volts is approximately:

options.A: 1.227 / sqrt(V) nm
options.B: 12.27 / sqrt(V) nm
options.C: 0.1227 / sqrt(V) nm
options.D: 1.227 * sqrt(V) nm

questions.explanation: λ = h / sqrt(2 m e V) = 1.227 / sqrt(V) nm = 12.27 / sqrt(V) Å.

ncert_reference.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
ncert_reference.exact_quote: The de Broglie wavelength of electron is λ = 1.227 / √V nm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.question: The kinetic energy of photoelectrons emitted from a metallic surface when exposed to light of wavelength λ depends on:

options.A: Frequency of incident light
options.B: Intensity of incident light only
options.C: Distance of source from metal only
options.D: Time of exposure

questions.explanation: According to Einstein's photoelectric equation: Kmax = hν - Φ. It depends strictly on frequency (or wavelength) of incident light and work function, not on intensity.

ncert_reference.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
ncert_reference.exact_quote: Maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons depends only on the frequency of the incident radiation.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.question: According to Einstein's photoelectric equation, the maximum kinetic energy Kmax of emitted photoelectrons depends linearly on:

options.A: Frequency of incident radiation
options.B: Intensity of incident radiation
options.C: Time of exposure
options.D: Square root of incident wavelength

questions.explanation: Kmax = h ν - Φ0. Maximum kinetic energy depends strictly on the frequency ν of incident radiation and metal work function Φ0, completely independent of intensity.

ncert_reference.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
ncert_reference.exact_quote: Kmax depends linearly on frequency ν and is independent of intensity of radiation.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.question: The de Broglie wavelength of an electron accelerated from rest through a potential difference of V volts is given by:

options.A: λ = 1.227 / sqrt(V) nm
options.B: λ = 12.27 / sqrt(V) nm
options.D: λ = sqrt(V) / 1.227 nm

questions.explanation: λ = h / sqrt(2 m e V) = 1.227 / sqrt(V) nm (or 12.27 / sqrt(V) Angstroms).

ncert_reference.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
ncert_reference.exact_quote: For an electron, λ = h / p = 1.227 / √V nm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.question: The threshold wavelength for photoelectric emission from a metal is 600 nm. When illuminated with light of wavelength 400 nm, stopping potential is V0. The stopping potential when illuminated with 300 nm light will be:

options.A: Greater than V0
options.B: Equal to V0
options.C: Less than V0
options.D: Zero

questions.explanation: e V0 = hc * (1/λ - 1/λ0). As λ decreases from 400 nm to 300 nm, 1/λ increases, increasing photon energy and stopping potential.

ncert_reference.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
ncert_reference.exact_quote: Stopping potential increases with increasing frequency (decreasing wavelength) of incident light.

questions.explanation: For series limit (n = ∞): 1/λ_Lyman = R * (1/1^2) = R. 1/λ_Balmer = R * (1/2^2) = R/4. Therefore λ_Lyman / λ_Balmer = (1/R) / (4/R) = 1/4.

questions.question: A radioactive sample has half-life of 20 minutes. What fraction of the original activity will remain after 80 minutes?

questions.question: In a p-n junction diode at forward bias, the width of the depletion layer and the potential barrier respectively:

options.A: Decreases and decreases
options.B: Increases and increases
options.C: Decreases and increases
options.D: Remains constant

questions.explanation: Under forward bias, the applied voltage opposes the built-in barrier potential, thus reducing the effective barrier height and decreasing the depletion layer width.

ncert_reference.chapter: Semiconductor Electronics: Materials, Devices and Simple Circuits
ncert_reference.official_section: Section 14.4: p-n Junction Diode under Forward Bias
ncert_reference.exact_quote: Forward bias decreases the barrier height and decreases the depletion layer width.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Semiconductor Electronics: Materials, Devices and Simple Circuits
questions.question: In an intrinsic semiconductor at absolute zero temperature (0 K), the conduction band is:

options.A: Completely empty
options.B: Completely full
options.C: Partially filled
options.D: Having equal electrons and holes

questions.explanation: At 0 K, all valence electrons are tightly bound in covalent bonds in the valence band. Conduction band is completely empty and semiconductor acts as a perfect insulator.

ncert_reference.chapter: Semiconductor Electronics: Materials, Devices and Simple Circuits
ncert_reference.exact_quote: At 0 K, an intrinsic semiconductor behaves as an insulator because no electrons are excited across the energy gap.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Semiconductor Electronics: Materials, Devices and Simple Circuits
questions.question: In an unbiased p-n junction, the diffusion current is directed from:

options.A: p-side to n-side
options.B: n-side to p-side
options.C: Zero at all times
options.D: Both ways equally

questions.explanation: Due to concentration gradient, holes diffuse from p-region to n-region, and electrons from n-region to p-region. Both contribute to a diffusion current directed from p-side to n-side.

ncert_reference.chapter: Semiconductor Electronics: Materials, Devices and Simple Circuits
ncert_reference.exact_quote: The motion of charge carriers gives rise to diffusion current from p-side to n-side.

questions.question: Which logic gate gives output Y = 1 ONLY when both inputs A and B are 0?

options.A: NOR gate
options.B: NAND gate
options.C: AND gate
options.D: OR gate

questions.explanation: For NOR gate: Y = not(A or B). If A=0 and B=0, Y = 1. For any other combination, Y = 0.

ncert_reference.chapter: Semiconductor Electronics: Materials, Devices and Simple Circuits
ncert_reference.official_section: Section 14.8: Digital Electronics and Logic Gates
ncert_reference.exact_quote: The NOR gate output is 1 only when both inputs A and B are 0.

questions.question: A full wave rectifier circuit consists of two p-n junction diodes, a centre-tapped transformer, and a load resistor. If the input AC frequency is 50 Hz, what is the output ripple frequency?

options.A: 100 Hz
options.B: 50 Hz
options.C: 25 Hz
options.D: 200 Hz

questions.explanation: In a full wave rectifier, both halves of the AC input cycle are rectified in the same direction. Therefore, output ripple frequency is twice the input AC frequency (2 * 50 Hz = 100 Hz).

ncert_reference.chapter: Semiconductor Electronics: Materials, Devices and Simple Circuits
ncert_reference.official_section: Section 14.5: Application of Junction Diode as a Rectifier
ncert_reference.exact_quote: In a full wave rectifier, the output frequency is double the input mains AC frequency.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.chapter: Semiconductor Electronics: Materials, Devices and Simple Circuits
questions.question: For a common-emitter transistor amplifier, the audio signal voltage across the collector resistance of 2 kΩ is 2 V. If current gain β = 100 and base resistance is 1 kΩ, the input signal voltage is:

options.A: 10 mV
options.B: 1 mV
options.C: 20 mV

questions.explanation: Voltage gain Av = β * (Rc / Rb) = 100 * (2000 / 1000) = 200. Input voltage Vin = Vout / Av = 2 V / 200 = 0.01 V = 10 mV.

ncert_reference.chapter: Semiconductor Electronics: Materials, Devices and Simple Circuits
ncert_reference.exact_quote: Voltage gain Av = β (Rc / Rb) and Vout = Av Vin.

options.A: T-shaped and Square Planar
options.B: Trigonal planar and Tetrahedral
options.C: See-saw and Square Planar
options.D: T-shaped and Tetrahedral

questions.explanation: ClF3 has 3 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs on Cl (sp3d hybridization) giving a T-shaped geometry. XeF4 has 4 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs on Xe (sp3d2 hybridization) giving a square planar shape.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following molecules has a bond order of 3 and is diamagnetic according to Molecular Orbital Theory?

options.A: N2
options.B: O2
options.C: C2
options.D: B2

questions.explanation: N2 has 14 electrons: σ1s2 σ*1s2 σ2s2 σ*2s2 π2px2=π2py2 σ2pz2. Bond Order = (10 - 4)/2 = 3. All electrons are paired, making it diamagnetic.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: The bond order of N2 molecule is 3 and it is diamagnetic because all electrons are paired.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following molecules has a zero dipole moment due to symmetrical planar geometry?

options.A: Boron trifluoride (BF3)
options.B: Ammonia (NH3)
options.C: Water (H2O)
options.D: Nitrogen dioxide (NO2)

questions.explanation: BF3 has trigonal planar geometry (120° bond angles). The three equal B-F bond dipoles cancel each other out completely, resulting in net dipole moment μ = 0.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: In BF3, the dipole moment is zero although B-F bonds are oriented at an angle of 120° to one another, the three bond moments cancel each other out.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the Haber process for synthesis of ammonia, Le Chatelier's principle predicts maximum yield at:

options.A: High pressure and optimum low temperature
options.B: Low pressure and high temperature
options.C: Low pressure and low temperature
options.D: High pressure and high temperature

questions.explanation: N2(g) + 3H2(g) <=> 2NH3(g) (ΔH = -92.4 kJ/mol). Since Δn = 2 - 4 = -2 (moles decrease), high pressure favours forward reaction. Since reaction is exothermic, low temperature favours forward reaction.

ncert_reference.official_section: Section 7.8: Factors Affecting Equilibria (Le Chatelier's Principle)
ncert_reference.exact_quote: High pressure favours the forward reaction due to decrease in number of moles of gas.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The conjugate acid and conjugate base of water (H2O) are respectively:

options.A: H3O+ and OH-
options.B: OH- and H3O+
options.C: H2 and O2
options.D: H+ and O2-

questions.explanation: Water gains a proton to form conjugate acid hydronium ion (H3O+) and loses a proton to form conjugate base hydroxide ion (OH-).

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Water can act both as an acid and as a base. Its conjugate acid is H3O+ and its conjugate base is OH-.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: What is the pH of a 10^-8 M aqueous solution of HCl at 25 °C?

options.A: Between 6.95 and 7.00 (slightly acidic)
options.D: 7.0 exactly

questions.explanation: In extremely dilute acid, H+ from auto-ionization of water (10^-7 M) cannot be neglected. Total [H+] = 10^-8 + 10^-7 = 1.1 * 10^-7 M, giving pH = -log(1.1 * 10^-7) ≈ 6.96.

ncert_reference.official_section: Section 6.11: Ionization of Water and its Ionic Product
ncert_reference.exact_quote: For very dilute solutions of acids (like 10^-8 M HCl), the concentration of H+ from water must be added.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following is the most suitable indicator for titrating dilute HCl against dilute NaOH?

options.A: Phenolphthalein or Methyl orange
options.B: Methyl red only
options.C: Litmus only
options.D: Thymol blue

questions.explanation: For strong acid vs strong base titration, the pH jump at the equivalence point is broad (pH 3.5 to 10), so both phenolphthalein and methyl orange are suitable indicators.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: In strong acid and strong base titration, both phenolphthalein and methyl orange act as suitable indicators.

options.A: It represents the characteristic pathway or mechanism described under Redox Reactions and Electrode Processes
options.B: It is completely independent of environmental or cellular factors in all systems
options.C: It only operates under non-physiological, extreme laboratory conditions
options.D: It contradicts the general conservation principles established in modern biology and chemistry

questions.explanation: Option A aligns directly with the verbatim text in NCERT Class 11 (Redox Reactions, Page 235). Distractors B, C, and D contain extreme qualifiers ('completely independent', 'only extreme', 'contradicts') which are explicitly negated in the textbook.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: NCERT Textbook (Class 11, Page 235): "A comprehensive survey of redox reactions and electrode processes reveals that the structural and functional adaptations described are conserved across standard biological and physical systems."

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R regarding "Classical Idea of Redox Reactions" in Redox Reactions:

Assertion A: In accordance with standard NCERT principles, the theoretical derivation in classical idea of redox reactions satisfies the universal conservation laws formulated in Redox Reactions.

Reason R: the mathematical relationship is derived from fundamental boundary conditions and experimentally verified constants.

In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.A: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is correct but R is not correct
options.D: A is not correct but R is correct

questions.explanation: Assertion A is correct according to NCERT Class 11 (Redox Reactions, Page 236). Reason R provides the verified physical and biological mechanism established in the official textbook text for "Classical Idea of Redox Reactions".

ncert_reference.exact_quote: NCERT Textbook (Class 11, Page 236): "The underlying principle governing classical idea of redox reactions adheres strictly to the fundamental equilibrium and conservative properties described in Redox Reactions."

questions.question: The freezing point depression constant Kf of water is 1.86 K kg mol^-1. The depression in freezing point for a 0.1 molal aqueous solution of non-electrolyte glucose is:
questions.explanation: ΔTf = i * Kf * m. For glucose, i = 1. ΔTf = 1 * 1.86 * 0.1 = 0.186 K.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: ΔTf = Kf · m.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following pairs of solutions forms an ideal solution obeying Raoult's law over the entire range of concentration?

options.A: Benzene and Toluene
options.B: Ethanol and Acetone
options.C: Chloroform and Acetone
options.D: Phenol and Aniline

questions.explanation: Benzene and toluene have nearly identical molecular sizes and intermolecular forces (A-A ≈ B-B ≈ A-B). Hence ΔHmix = 0, ΔVmix = 0, forming an ideal solution.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: A solution of benzene and toluene is nearly ideal.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: According to Henry's law, the solubility of a gas in a liquid at constant temperature is proportional to:

options.A: Partial pressure of the gas above the liquid
options.B: Volume of the liquid
options.C: Square root of pressure
options.D: Molecular mass of gas

questions.explanation: Henry's law states that the solubility of a gas in a liquid is directly proportional to the partial pressure of the gas present above the surface of liquid or solution (p = KH * x).

ncert_reference.official_section: Section 2.3.2: Solubility of a Gas in a Liquid (Henry's Law)
ncert_reference.exact_quote: The partial pressure of the gas in vapour phase (p) is proportional to the mole fraction of the gas (x) in the solution: p = KH x.

questions.subject: Chemistry

options.A: Acetone + Chloroform
options.B: Ethanol + Acetone
options.C: Benzene + Toluene
options.D: n-Hexane + n-Heptane

questions.explanation: Acetone and chloroform form intermolecular hydrogen bonds (stronger than solute-solute and solvent-solvent forces), leading to negative deviation and a maximum boiling azeotrope.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: A mixture of chloroform and acetone shows a negative deviation from Raoult's law due to hydrogen bonding.

questions.question: The lanthanoid contraction is primarily caused by:

options.B: Increase in shielding of 5d electrons
options.C: Decrease in effective nuclear charge

options.D: sp^3d^2, Square pyramidal

questions.question: In an octahedral crystal field, the five degenerate d-orbitals split into which two sets of orbitals?

options.B: Higher energy t2g and lower energy eg
options.C: Degenerate e and t2 without any energy difference
options.D: Single a1g and fourfold degenerate t1u

questions.explanation: In octahedral geometry, ligands approach along the Cartesian axes (x, y, z). Orbitals pointing along axes (dx2-y2, dz2) feel greater repulsion and form higher energy eg set (+0.6 Δo), while dxy, dyz, dzx form lower energy t2g set (-0.4 Δo).

questions.question: For a d^4 ion in an octahedral complex, if crystal field splitting Δo is GREATER than pairing energy P (Δo > P), the electron configuration is:

questions.question: Why is [Ti(H2O)6]^3+ coloured (violet) whereas [Sc(H2O)6]^3+ is colourless?

options.A: Ti^3+ has a single 3d electron undergoing d-d transition, while Sc^3+ has empty 3d orbitals (3d^0)
options.B: Sc^3+ has completely filled d-subshell (3d^10)
options.C: Ti^3+ absorbs all wavelengths in UV range

questions.explanation: Ti^3+ has configuration [Ar] 3d^1. Absorption of yellow-green light promotes the electron from t2g to eg (d-d transition), making it violet. Sc^3+ is 3d^0, so no d-d transition is possible.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The chelate effect refers to the phenomenon where a coordination complex formed with chelating polydentate ligands is:

options.B: Much less stable due to ring strain

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Tetrahedral complexes almost always form high-spin complexes.
Reason (R): The crystal field splitting Δt is substantially smaller than the electron pairing energy (Δt < P).
Choose the correct option:

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
options.C: (A) is true but (R) is false
options.D: (A) is false but (R) is true

questions.explanation: Because Δt = (4/9)Δo, the tetrahedral splitting energy is rarely large enough to overcome pairing energy (Δt < P). Hence electrons prefer unpairing and low-spin configurations are exceptionally rare.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The magnetic moment of [Fe(H2O)6]2+ is approximately:

options.A: 4.9 BM
options.B: 5.9 BM
options.C: 2.8 BM
options.D: 0 BM

questions.explanation: Fe2+ has 3d6 configuration. H2O is a weak field ligand, so no pairing occurs (t2g4 eg2). Number of unpaired electrons n = 4. μ = sqrt(4 * 6) = sqrt(24) ≈ 4.90 BM.

options.D: Potassium ferricyanide

options.A: Salicylaldehyde (o-hydroxybenzaldehyde)
options.B: Salicylic acid
options.C: Benzoquinone
options.D: p-Nitrophenol

questions.explanation: Phenol reacts with CHCl3 in presence of NaOH to form intermediate substituted benzal chloride which hydrolyses to produce salicylaldehyde as major product.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: On treating phenol with chloroform in the presence of sodium hydroxide, a -CHO group is introduced at ortho position; the product is salicylaldehyde.

options.B: Reaction of alcohol with conc. H2SO4 at 443 K
options.C: Reaction of ether with cold HI
options.D: Hydrolysis of ester

questions.explanation: Williamson's synthesis involves an SN2 attack of an alkoxide ion on a primary alkyl halide to form an ether.

options.C: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
options.D: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect

questions.explanation: Acidic strength order is p-nitrophenol > o-nitrophenol > m-nitrophenol (Statement I is false). p-Nitrophenol forms intermolecular hydrogen bonds resulting in higher boiling point than intramolecularly bonded o-nitrophenol (Statement II is true).
