questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Rosenmund reduction of benzoyl chloride to benzaldehyde is carried out using which catalyst?

options.A: H2 in the presence of Pd-BaSO4 (poisoned by sulfur or quinoline)
options.B: SnCl2 + HCl (Stephen reaction)
options.C: DIBAL-H in toluene at -78 °C
options.D: CrO2Cl2 in CS2 (Etard reaction)

questions.explanation: Acyl chlorides (acid chlorides) are hydrogenated over catalyst palladium on barium sulphate (Pd-BaSO4) to give aldehydes. This reaction is called Rosenmund reduction.

ncert_reference.official_section: Section 12.2.1: Preparation of Aldehydes (From acyl chloride)
ncert_reference.exact_quote: Acyl chloride is hydrogenated over catalyst, palladium on barium sulphate. This reaction is called Rosenmund reduction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Chromyl chloride (CrO2Cl2) oxidizes the methyl group of toluene to a brown chromium complex, which on acidic hydrolysis yields benzaldehyde. This reaction is named:

options.A: Etard reaction
options.B: Gatterman-Koch reaction
options.C: Stephen reaction
options.D: Cannizzaro reaction

questions.explanation: Chromyl chloride oxidises methyl group to a chromium complex, which on hydrolysis gives corresponding benzaldehyde. This reaction is known as Etard reaction.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Chromyl chloride oxidises methyl group to a chromium complex, which on hydrolysis gives corresponding benzaldehyde. This reaction is called Etard reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: When benzene or its derivative is treated with carbon monoxide (CO) and HCl in the presence of anhydrous AlCl3 / CuCl, benzaldehyde is formed. This is:

options.A: Gatterman-Koch reaction
options.B: Friedel-Crafts acylation
options.C: Rosenmund reaction
options.D: Reimer-Tiemann reaction

questions.explanation: When benzene or its derivative is treated with carbon monoxide and hydrogen chloride in the presence of anhydrous aluminium chloride or cuprous chloride, it gives benzaldehyde or substituted benzaldehyde. This reaction is known as Gatterman-Koch reaction.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: This reaction is known as Gatterman-Koch reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following carbonyl compounds is MOST reactive toward nucleophilic addition reactions?

options.A: HCHO (Formaldehyde)
options.B: CH3CHO (Acetaldehyde)
options.C: CH3COCH3 (Acetone)
options.D: C6H5COCH3 (Acetophenone)

questions.explanation: Aldehydes are more reactive than ketones due to steric and electronic factors. Formaldehyde (HCHO) has no alkyl groups (+I effect and steric hindrance), making its carbonyl carbon most electrophilic.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Aldehydes are generally more reactive than ketones in nucleophilic addition reactions due to steric and electronic reasons.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Tollens' reagent used to distinguish aldehydes from ketones is chemically:

options.A: Ammoniacal silver nitrate solution [Ag(NH3)2]+ OH-
options.B: Alkaline solution of copper sulfate with sodium potassium tartrate
options.C: Acidified potassium dichromate solution
options.D: Neutral ferric chloride solution

questions.explanation: Tollens' reagent is freshly prepared ammoniacal silver nitrate solution. On warming an aldehyde with Tollens' reagent, a bright silver mirror is produced due to the formation of silver metal.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Tollens' test: On warming an aldehyde with freshly prepared ammoniacal silver nitrate solution (Tollens' reagent), a bright silver mirror is produced.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following compounds gives a positive Fehling's test (red precipitate of Cu2O)?

options.A: Acetaldehyde (CH3CHO)
options.B: Benzaldehyde (C6H5CHO)
options.C: Acetophenone (C6H5COCH3)
options.D: Benzophenone (C6H5COC6H5)

questions.explanation: Aliphatic aldehydes reduce Fehling's solution to red Cu2O. Aromatic aldehydes (like benzaldehyde) do NOT reduce Fehling's solution.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Fehling's test: Aromatic aldehydes do not reduce Fehling's solution.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The iodoform test (treatment with NaOH and I2 giving a yellow precipitate of CHI3) is given by compounds containing which structural unit?

options.A: CH3-C=O or CH3-CH(OH)- group
options.B: -COOH group only
options.C: -CH2-CH2-OH group only
options.D: Phenolic -OH group

questions.explanation: Aldehydes and ketones having at least one methyl group linked to the carbonyl carbon (methyl ketones) or alcohols having CH3-CH(OH)- group are oxidised by sodium hypohalite to give yellow precipitate of iodoform (CHI3).

ncert_reference.official_section: Section 12.4.2: Oxidation of Methyl Ketones (Haloform reaction)
ncert_reference.exact_quote: Aldehydes and ketones having at least one methyl group linked to the carbonyl carbon atom (methyl ketones) are oxidised by sodium hypohalite to sodium salts of corresponding carboxylic acids... and yellow precipitate of iodoform.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following will NOT give a yellow precipitate on treatment with I2 and aqueous NaOH?

options.A: Benzophenone (C6H5-CO-C6H5)
options.B: Acetone (CH3-CO-CH3)
options.C: Acetaldehyde (CH3-CHO)
options.D: Acetophenone (C6H5-CO-CH3)

questions.explanation: Benzophenone lacks any methyl carbonyl group (-CO-CH3), so it fails the iodoform test. Acetone, acetaldehyde, and acetophenone all have the -CO-CH3 group and yield yellow CHI3.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Benzophenone does not contain a methyl ketone moiety and therefore gives negative haloform test.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Aldehydes having NO alpha-hydrogen atoms undergo self-oxidation and reduction (disproportionation) when heated with concentrated alkali. This reaction is known as:

options.A: Cannizzaro reaction
options.B: Aldol condensation
options.C: Clemmensen reduction
options.D: Wolff-Kishner reduction

questions.explanation: Aldehydes which do not have an alpha-hydrogen atom undergo self-oxidation and reduction (disproportionation) on treatment with concentrated alkali. This is known as Cannizzaro reaction.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Aldehydes which do not have an alpha-hydrogen atom, undergo self-oxidation and reduction (disproportionation) reaction on heating with concentrated alkali. This reaction is called Cannizzaro reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: When formaldehyde (HCHO) is heated with 50% concentrated NaOH, what are the products formed in the Cannizzaro reaction?

options.A: Methanol (CH3OH) and Sodium formate (HCOONa)
options.B: Formic acid and Ethanol
options.C: Acetaldehyde and Water
options.D: Sodium acetate and Carbon dioxide

questions.explanation: In the Cannizzaro reaction of formaldehyde: 2 HCHO + conc. NaOH -> CH3OH (reduced alcohol) + HCOONa (oxidized carboxylate salt).

ncert_reference.exact_quote: 2 HCHO + conc. KOH -> CH3OH + HCOOK.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Reduction of the carbonyl group (>C=O) of aldehydes or ketones to methylene (>CH2) using zinc amalgam (Zn-Hg) and concentrated HCl is called:

options.A: Clemmensen reduction
options.B: Wolff-Kishner reduction
options.C: Rosenmund reduction
options.D: Stephen reduction

questions.explanation: The carbonyl group of aldehydes and ketones is reduced to -CH2- group on treatment with zinc-amalgam and concentrated hydrochloric acid (Clemmensen reduction).

ncert_reference.exact_quote: The carbonyl group of aldehydes and ketones is reduced to CH2 group on treatment with zinc-amalgam and concentrated hydrochloric acid [Clemmensen reduction].

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Wolff-Kishner reduction converts a carbonyl group into a methylene group (>CH2) using which reagent combination?

options.A: Hydrazine (NH2-NH2) followed by heating with KOH in ethylene glycol
options.B: Zn-Hg and concentrated HCl
options.C: LiAlH4 in dry ether
options.D: H2 with Raney nickel

questions.explanation: Carbonyl compounds react with hydrazine to form hydrazones, which on heating with sodium or potassium hydroxide in high-boiling solvent like ethylene glycol yield alkanes (Wolff-Kishner reduction).

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Treatment with hydrazine followed by heating with sodium or potassium hydroxide in high boiling solvent such as ethylene glycol [Wolff-Kishner reduction].

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Why do carboxylic acids have higher boiling points than alcohols of comparable molecular mass?

options.A: Carboxylic acids form extensive intermolecular hydrogen bonding and exist as stable cyclic dimers
options.B: Carboxylic acids have higher covalent bond energy
options.C: Alcohols cannot form hydrogen bonds
options.D: Carboxylic acids are non-polar molecules

questions.explanation: Carboxylic acids have higher boiling points because their molecules are held together by two strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds, existing as stable cyclic dimers even in the vapour phase.

ncert_reference.official_section: Section 12.7: Physical Properties of Carboxylic Acids
ncert_reference.exact_quote: Carboxylic acids are higher boiling liquids than aldehydes, ketones and even alcohols of comparable molecular masses. This is due to more extensive association of carboxylic acid molecules through intermolecular hydrogen bonding... cyclic dimers.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following substituted acetic acids is the STRONGEST acid?

options.A: CF3COOH (Trifluoroacetic acid)
options.B: CCl3COOH (Trichloroacetic acid)
options.C: CH2FCOOH (Fluoroacetic acid)
options.D: CH3COOH (Acetic acid)

questions.explanation: Electron-withdrawing groups (-I effect) stabilize the carboxylate anion by dispersing negative charge. Three strongly electronegative fluorine atoms in CF3COOH exert an exceptionally strong -I effect, making it the strongest acid.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: The effect of the following groups in increasing the acidity order is: CF3 > CCl3 > CHCl2 > NO2 > CN > F > Cl > Br > I > Ph.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Carboxylic acids having an alpha-hydrogen react with chlorine or bromine in the presence of small amounts of red phosphorus to give alpha-halocarboxylic acids. This reaction is:

options.A: Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (HVZ) reaction
options.B: Hunsdiecker reaction
options.C: Kolbe electrolysis
options.D: Etard reaction

questions.explanation: Carboxylic acids having an alpha-hydrogen are halogenated at the alpha-position on treatment with chlorine or bromine in the presence of small amount of red phosphorus to give alpha-halocarboxylic acids (HVZ reaction).

ncert_reference.exact_quote: This reaction is known as Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reaction.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the Aldol condensation of acetaldehyde with dilute NaOH, the product initially formed before heating is:

options.A: 3-Hydroxybutanal (beta-hydroxy aldehyde)
options.B: But-2-enal (crotonaldehyde)
options.C: 2-Hydroxybutanal
options.D: Butan-1-ol

questions.explanation: Acetaldehyde reacts with dilute NaOH to form 3-hydroxybutanal (aldol), containing both an aldehyde and alcohol group. On subsequent heating, it loses water to form but-2-enal.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: 2 CH3-CHO --(dil NaOH)--> CH3-CH(OH)-CH2-CHO (3-Hydroxybutanal / Aldol).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: When sodium salt of a carboxylic acid is heated with soda lime (NaOH + CaO in 3:1 ratio), it undergoes decarboxylation to produce an alkane with:

options.A: One carbon atom less than the parent carboxylic acid
options.B: The same number of carbon atoms
options.C: Double the number of carbon atoms
options.D: One carbon atom more

questions.explanation: Decarboxylation with soda lime removes carbon dioxide as carbonate (Na2CO3), producing an alkane with one less carbon atom than the parent carboxylic acid salt.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Carboxylic acids lose carbon dioxide to form hydrocarbons when their sodium salts are heated with sodalime. The reaction is known as decarboxylation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Kolbe's electrolytic decarboxylation of potassium acetate (CH3COOK) in aqueous solution produces which gas at the anode?

options.A: Ethane (C2H6) and CO2
options.B: Methane (CH4) and O2
options.C: Hydrogen (H2) only
options.D: Ethene (C2H4) and CO

questions.explanation: An aqueous solution of sodium or potassium salt of a carboxylic acid on electrolysis gives alkane having even number of carbon atoms. At anode: 2 CH3COO- -> C2H6 + 2 CO2 + 2 e-.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: An aqueous solution of sodium or potassium salt of a carboxylic acid on electrolysis gives alkane having even number of carbon atoms (Kolbe electrolysis).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Carboxylic acids do NOT give the characteristic nucleophilic addition reactions of the carbonyl group (>C=O) because:

options.A: The carbonyl carbon is involved in resonance with the adjacent hydroxyl oxygen, reducing its electrophilicity
options.B: Carboxylic acids are insoluble in polar solvents
options.C: The carbonyl bond in carboxylic acids is triple bonded
options.D: Hydroxyl group completely hydrolyzes nucleophiles

questions.explanation: In carboxylic acids, resonance donation of lone pairs from the -OH oxygen to the carbonyl group reduces the partial positive charge on the carbonyl carbon, making it much less electrophilic than in aldehydes and ketones.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: The carbonyl carbon in carboxylic acids is less electrophilic than in aldehydes and ketones because of the resonance contribution of the lone pair of electrons from the hydroxyl oxygen.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which reagent converts acetic acid directly into acetyl chloride?

options.A: Thionyl chloride (SOCl2)
options.B: Dilute HCl
options.C: Sodium chloride (NaCl)
options.D: Chlorine gas in water

questions.explanation: Carboxylic acids react with PCl5, PCl3, or SOCl2 to form acid chlorides. SOCl2 is preferred because the by-products (SO2 and HCl) are gases and escape easily, leaving pure acid chloride.

ncert_reference.official_section: Section 12.8.2: Reactions with PCl5, PCl3 and SOCl2
ncert_reference.exact_quote: Thionyl chloride (SOCl2) is preferred because other two products are gaseous and escape the reaction mixture leaving behind the pure product.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: When benzoic acid is treated with bromine in the presence of FeBr3, the major product is:

options.A: m-Bromobenzoic acid
options.B: o-Bromobenzoic acid
options.C: p-Bromobenzoic acid
options.D: 2,4-Dibromobenzoic acid

questions.explanation: The carboxyl group (-COOH) is a strongly electron-withdrawing deactivating group that directs electrophilic aromatic substitution to the meta-position.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Carboxyl group acts as a deactivating and meta-directing group. Benzoic acid on bromination gives m-bromobenzoic acid.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Why do aromatic carboxylic acids NOT undergo Friedel-Crafts alkylation or acylation reactions?

options.A: Because the -COOH group is strongly deactivating and the catalyst AlCl3 binds to the carboxyl group as a Lewis base
options.B: Because benzoic acid is insoluble in AlCl3
options.C: Because aromatic ring has excess electron density
options.D: Because benzene ring decomposes in acid

questions.explanation: Benzoic acid does not undergo Friedel-Crafts reaction because the -COOH group is strongly deactivating and the Lewis acid catalyst AlCl3 coordinates strongly to the carboxyl group.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: They do not undergo Friedel-Crafts reaction because the carboxyl group is deactivating and the catalyst aluminium chloride (Lewis acid) gets bonded to the carboxyl group.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following compounds gives a positive Brady's test (yellow-orange precipitate with 2,4-DNP)?

options.A: Both aldehydes and ketones
options.B: Carboxylic acids only
options.C: Esters only
options.D: Alcohols only

questions.explanation: 2,4-Dinitrophenylhydrazine (2,4-DNP or Brady's reagent) reacts with aldehydes and ketones to give bright yellow, orange, or red hydrazone precipitates, used as a qualitative test for carbonyl compounds.

ncert_reference.official_section: Section 12.4.1: Addition of Ammonia Derivatives (2,4-DNP Derivatives)
ncert_reference.exact_quote: 2,4-DNP-derivatives are yellow, orange or red solids, useful for characterisation of aldehydes and ketones.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Acetal formation from an aldehyde involves reversible reaction with two equivalents of monohydric alcohol in the presence of:

options.A: Dry HCl gas (acid catalyst)
options.B: Concentrated NaOH
options.C: Pyridine
options.D: Anhydrous AlCl3

questions.explanation: Aldehydes react with one equivalent of monohydric alcohol in the presence of dry hydrogen chloride to yield hemiacetals, which react with another alcohol molecule to form stable gem-dialkoxy compounds known as acetals.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Dry hydrogen chloride protonates the oxygen of the carbonyl compound and therefore, increases the electrophilicity of the carbonyl carbon.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Ketones react with ethylene glycol in the presence of dry HCl to form cyclic ketals known as:

options.A: Ethylene glycol ketals (1,3-dioxolanes)
options.B: Hemiacetals
options.C: Enamines
options.D: Oximes

questions.explanation: Ketones react with ethylene glycol under similar conditions to form cyclic products known as ethylene glycol ketals (useful as protecting groups).

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Ketones react with ethylene glycol under similar conditions to form cyclic products known as ethylene glycol ketals.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Addition of sodium hydrogen sulphite (NaHSO3) to an aldehyde produces a white crystalline bisulphite addition product that is useful for:

options.A: Purification and separation of aldehydes from non-carbonyl impurities
options.B: Determining degree of unsaturation
options.C: Oxidizing aldehyde to acid
options.D: Reducing aldehyde to alkane

questions.explanation: The bisulphite addition compound is water-soluble crystalline solid and can be converted back to the original carbonyl compound by treating it with dilute mineral acid or alkali, making it ideal for purification.

ncert_reference.official_section: Section 12.4.1: Addition of Sodium Hydrogen Sulphite
ncert_reference.exact_quote: The hydrogen sulphite addition compound is water soluble and can be converted back to the original carbonyl compound... Therefore, these are useful for separation and purification of aldehydes.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following dicarboxylic acids on heating readily undergoes intramolecular dehydration to form a cyclic anhydride?

options.A: Phthalic acid (benzene-1,2-dicarboxylic acid)
options.B: Terephthalic acid (benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid)
options.C: Oxalic acid
options.D: Formic acid

questions.explanation: Phthalic acid has two carboxyl groups on adjacent ortho carbons, allowing easy loss of water on heating to form stable 5-membered cyclic phthalic anhydride.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Phthalic acid on heating loses water to yield phthalic anhydride.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the reaction of an aldehyde with hydroxylamine (NH2OH), what class of organic nitrogen derivative is obtained?

options.A: Oxime
options.B: Hydrazone
options.C: Semicarbazone
options.D: Schiff's base

questions.explanation: Aldehydes and ketones react with hydroxylamine (NH2OH) with elimination of water to form oximes (>C=N-OH).

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Reagent: Hydroxylamine (NH2OH) -> Carbonyl derivative: Oxime (>C=N-OH).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Treatment of benzaldehyde with concentrated NaOH yields benzyl alcohol and sodium benzoate. This is an example of:

options.A: Crossed Aldol condensation
options.B: Cannizzaro reaction
options.C: Kolbe reaction
options.D: Friedel-Crafts reaction

questions.explanation: Benzaldehyde has no alpha-hydrogen atom. On heating with concentrated NaOH, one molecule is reduced to benzyl alcohol and the other is oxidized to sodium benzoate (Cannizzaro reaction).

ncert_reference.exact_quote: 2 C6H5CHO + conc. NaOH -> C6H5CH2OH + C6H5COONa.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following organic acids gives effervescence of CO2 gas with aqueous sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3)?

options.A: Benzoic acid
options.B: Phenol
options.C: Ethanol
options.D: Acetone

questions.explanation: Carboxylic acids (pKa ~ 4-5) are stronger acids than carbonic acid (pKa ~ 6.4) and decompose aqueous NaHCO3 to liberate CO2 gas with brisk effervescence. Phenol and alcohols are weaker acids and do not give this test.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Carboxylic acids react with sodium hydrogen carbonate and liberate brisk effervescence of carbon dioxide gas. This reaction is used to distinguish carboxylic acids from phenols.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following organic compounds gives a positive iodoform test (forms yellow precipitate of CHI3 with I2 + NaOH)?

options.A: Pentan-2-one
options.B: Pentan-3-one
options.C: Benzaldehyde
options.D: Methanol

questions.explanation: Compounds containing the CH3-C=O or CH3-CH(OH)- group give positive iodoform test. Pentan-2-one is a methyl ketone (CH3-CO-CH2-CH2-CH3), whereas pentan-3-one does not possess a terminal methyl ketone.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Aldehydes and ketones having at least one methyl group linked to the carbonyl carbon atom are oxidized by sodium hypohalite to give haloform.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Cannizzaro reaction is not shown by which of the following carbonyl compounds?

options.A: Acetaldehyde (CH3CHO)
options.B: Formaldehyde (HCHO)
options.C: Benzaldehyde (C6H5CHO)
options.D: Trimethylacetaldehyde ((CH3)3CCHO)

questions.explanation: Cannizzaro reaction is given by aldehydes which do NOT possess α-hydrogen atoms. Acetaldehyde has 3 α-hydrogens and instead undergoes aldol condensation.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Aldehydes which do not have an α-hydrogen atom undergo self-oxidation and reduction on heating with concentrated alkali (Cannizzaro reaction).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: In the reaction: R-COOH + PCl5 -> X + POCl3 + HCl, the organic product X is:

options.A: Acyl chloride (R-COCl)
options.B: Alkyl chloride (R-Cl)
options.C: Acid anhydride ((RCO)2O)
options.D: Ester (R-COOR)

questions.explanation: Carboxylic acids react with PCl5 to produce acyl chloride (R-COCl), phosphoryl chloride (POCl3) and hydrogen chloride (HCl).

ncert_reference.official_section: Section 12.8: Reactions Involving Cleavage of C-OH Bond
ncert_reference.exact_quote: Carboxylic acids react with PCl5, PCl3 or SOCl2 to form acid chlorides.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The IUPAC name of the compound CH3-CH(OH)-CH2-COOH is:

options.A: 3-Hydroxybutanoic acid
options.B: 2-Hydroxybutanoic acid
options.C: 4-Hydroxybutanoic acid
options.D: 3-Hydroxypentanoic acid

questions.explanation: Numbering starts from carboxylic carbon C1: C1 is -COOH, C2 is -CH2-, C3 has -OH substituent, C4 is -CH3. Name: 3-hydroxybutanoic acid.

ncert_reference.official_section: Section 12.6: Nomenclature and Structure of Carboxyl Group
ncert_reference.exact_quote: In naming carboxylic acids containing hydroxy group, the principal functional group -COOH receives priority C1.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is exclusively used for the preparation of:

options.A: Primary aliphatic amines
options.B: Aromatic primary amines (Aniline)
options.C: Secondary amines
options.D: Tertiary amines

questions.explanation: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis produces pure primary aliphatic amines. Aryl halides cannot be used because they do not undergo nucleophilic substitution with phthalimide anion.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is used for the preparation of aliphatic primary amines. Aromatic primary amines cannot be prepared by this method.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which gas is evolved when primary aliphatic amine reacts with nitrous acid (HNO2) at 0-5°C?

options.A: Nitrogen gas (N2) quantitatively
options.B: Ammonia (NH3)
options.C: Nitric oxide (NO)
options.D: Nitrogen dioxide (NO2)

questions.explanation: Primary aliphatic amines react with nitrous acid to form unstable aliphatic diazonium salts, which decompose immediately to release nitrogen gas (N2) quantitatively and form alcohols.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Primary aliphatic amines react with nitrous acid to form aliphatic diazonium salts, which being unstable, liberate nitrogen gas quantitatively.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Hoffmann bromamide degradation of an amide produces a primary amine with:

options.A: One carbon atom less than the parent amide
options.B: The same number of carbon atoms
options.C: One carbon atom more
options.D: Double the number of carbons

questions.explanation: R-CONH2 + Br2 + 4 NaOH -> R-NH2 + Na2CO3 + 2 NaBr + 2 H2O. The amine formed has one carbon atom less than the starting amide.

ncert_reference.official_section: Section 13.3: Preparation of Amines (Hoffmann Bromamide Degradation)
ncert_reference.exact_quote: The amine so formed contains one carbon less than that present in the amide.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following amine will give the carbylamine test with chloroform and ethanolic KOH?

options.A: Aniline (Primary amine)
options.B: N-Methylaniline (Secondary amine)
options.C: N,N-Dimethylaniline (Tertiary amine)
options.D: Diethylamine (Secondary amine)

questions.explanation: The carbylamine test (isocyanide test) is given ONLY by primary aliphatic and aromatic amines. Aniline is a primary aromatic amine and yields foul-smelling phenyl isocyanide.

ncert_reference.official_section: Section 13.6: Chemical Reactions of Amines (Carbylamine reaction)
ncert_reference.exact_quote: Aliphatic and aromatic primary amines on heating with chloroform and ethanolic potassium hydroxide form isocyanides or carbylamines.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following statements is strictly correct regarding "Structure and Classification of Amines" as explicitly detailed in NCERT Class 12 (Amines)?

options.A: It represents the characteristic pathway or mechanism described under Structure and Classification of Amines
options.B: It is completely independent of environmental or cellular factors in all systems

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following vitamins is water-soluble and excreted in urine?

options.A: Vitamin C (Ascorbic acid)
options.B: Vitamin A
options.C: Vitamin D
options.D: Vitamin K

questions.explanation: B group vitamins and Vitamin C are water-soluble. They are excreted readily in urine and must be supplied regularly in diet. Vitamins A, D, E, K are fat-soluble.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Water soluble vitamins must be supplied regularly in diet because they are readily excreted in urine.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: Which of the following carbohydrates is a non-reducing disaccharide?

options.A: Sucrose
options.B: Maltose
options.C: Lactose
options.D: Cellobiose

questions.explanation: In sucrose, reducing groups of both glucose (C1) and fructose (C2) are involved in glycosidic bond formation, making it a non-reducing sugar.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Since the reducing groups of glucose and fructose are involved in glycosidic bond formation, sucrose is a non-reducing sugar.

options.A: Vitamin C and Vitamin B complex
options.B: Vitamin A
options.C: Vitamin D
options.D: Vitamin K

questions.explanation: B group vitamins and vitamin C are water soluble. Water soluble vitamins must be supplied regularly in diet because they are readily excreted in urine and cannot be stored.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: B group vitamins and vitamin C are soluble in water. Water soluble vitamins must be supplied regularly in diet because they are readily excreted in urine.

options.B: 2n (Diploid)

options.D: 4n (Tetraploid)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: In C4 plants, the primary CO2 acceptor and the first stable photosynthetic product are respectively:

options.A: Phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP) and Oxaloacetic acid (OAA)
options.B: RuBP and 3-PGA
options.C: PEP and Malic acid
options.D: RuBP and Oxaloacetic acid

questions.explanation: In mesophyll cells of C4 plants, primary CO2 acceptor is 3-carbon PEP, catalyzed by PEP carboxylase, forming 4-carbon OAA as the first stable product.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: The primary CO2 acceptor is a 3-carbon molecule phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP) and is present in the mesophyll cells. The C4 acid OAA is formed.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: Kranz anatomy is a characteristic anatomical feature of leaves of:

options.A: C4 plants like Maize and Sugarcane
options.B: C3 plants like Rice and Wheat
options.C: CAM plants like Pineapple
options.D: Hydrophytes

questions.explanation: Kranz anatomy (wreath-like arrangement of large bundle sheath cells with agranal chloroplasts surrounding vascular bundles) is unique to C4 plants.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: The bundle sheath cells may form several layers around the vascular bundles; they have a large number of chloroplasts, thick walls impervious to gaseous exchange and no intercellular spaces. This anatomy is Kranz anatomy.

options.B: Magnesium (Mg) and Iron (Fe)
options.C: Zinc (Zn) and Copper (Cu)
options.D: Molybdenum (Mo) and Boron (B)

questions.explanation: Photolysis of water (splitting of water into H+, e-, and O2) is catalyzed by an oxygen-evolving complex containing Manganese (Mn2+) and Chlorine (Cl-).

ncert_reference.exact_quote: The water splitting complex is associated with PS II... Manganese and chlorine ions play a crucial role in water splitting.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: During non-cyclic photophosphorylation in light reaction of photosynthesis, the primary electron acceptor from Photosystem II is a:

options.A: Pheophytin
options.B: Plastocyanin
options.C: Ferredoxin
options.D: Cytochrome b6f

questions.explanation: In PS II (P680), light energy excites electrons which are transferred to an electron acceptor, specifically pheophytin, before moving down the electron transport chain.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Electrons from excited PS II are transferred to an electron acceptor which passes them to an electron transport system.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: In C4 plants, the primary CO2 acceptor and the first stable photosynthetic product in mesophyll cells are respectively:

options.A: Phosphoenolpyruvate (PEP) and Oxaloacetic acid (OAA)
options.B: RuBP and 3-PGA
options.C: Pyruvate and Malic acid
options.D: RuBP and Oxaloacetic acid

questions.explanation: In C4 pathway, PEP (3-carbon molecule) is the primary CO2 acceptor in mesophyll cells catalysed by PEP carboxylase, forming 4-carbon oxaloacetic acid (OAA).

ncert_reference.exact_quote: The primary CO2 acceptor is a 3-carbon molecule phosphoenol pyruvate (PEP) and the first stable product is oxaloacetic acid (OAA).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: How many ATP and NADPH molecules are required for the synthesis of ONE molecule of glucose in the Calvin cycle (C3 pathway)?

options.A: 18 ATP and 12 NADPH
options.B: 12 ATP and 18 NADPH
options.C: 30 ATP and 12 NADPH
options.D: 38 ATP and 10 NADPH

questions.explanation: For each CO2 molecule fixed, 3 ATP and 2 NADPH are consumed. For 1 glucose (6 CO2): 6 * 3 = 18 ATP and 6 * 2 = 12 NADPH.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: To make one molecule of glucose 6 turns of the cycle are required. 18 ATP and 12 NADPH are required.

options.B: 2 meiotic divisions

options.C: Fertilization of synergids by male gametes

questions.explanation: Syngamy produces diploid zygote (2n), while triple fusion with two polar nuclei produces triploid Primary Endosperm Nucleus (PEN, 3n). This unique event is double fertilization.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Since two types of fusions, syngamy and triple fusion take place in an embryo sac the phenomenon is termed double fertilisation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: In Antirrhinum majus (snapdragon), a cross between red flower (RR) and white flower (rr) yielded pink flower (Rr) in F1. When F1 was self-pollinated, what was the phenotypic and genotypic ratio in F2?

options.A: 1 Red : 2 Pink : 1 White (both phenotypic and genotypic ratios are 1:2:1)
options.B: 3 Red : 1 White phenotypic ratio, 1:2:1 genotypic ratio
options.C: 9:3:3:1 ratio for both
options.D: All pink flowers

questions.explanation: In incomplete dominance in snapdragon, the phenotypic ratio 1:2:1 completely matches the genotypic ratio (1 RR : 2 Rr : 1 rr), because heterozygote Rr produces intermediate pink pigment.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Here the phenotypic ratio was 1:2:1 (1 Red : 2 Pink : 1 White), which is completely identical to the genotypic ratio.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question:
Assertion (A): ABO blood grouping in humans is a classical example of multiple allelism and codominance.
Reason (R): In ABO blood groups, alleles IA and IB both express their own types of sugars completely when present together.
Choose the correct option:

options.A: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
options.B: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
options.C: (A) is true but (R) is false
options.D: (A) is false but (R) is true

questions.explanation: Because there are three alleles (IA, IB, i) in human population, it exhibits multiple allelism. When IA and IB are present together (IAIB), both enzymes produce their respective sugars, demonstrating codominance.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: When IA and IB are present together that is in an individual of genotype IAIB, both enzymes produce their own sugars, this is co-dominance.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: What is the total number of possible genotypes and phenotypes respectively for human ABO blood groups controlled by three alleles?

options.A: 6 genotypes and 4 phenotypes
options.B: 4 genotypes and 6 phenotypes
options.C: 3 genotypes and 3 phenotypes
options.D: 9 genotypes and 4 phenotypes

questions.explanation: With 3 alleles, total genotypes = n(n+1)/2 = 3(4)/2 = 6 genotypes (IAIA, IAi, IBIB, IBi, IAIB, ii) which yield 4 phenotypes (Blood group A, B, AB, O).

ncert_reference.exact_quote: There are six different combinations of these three alleles that are possible, and therefore a total of six different genotypes of the human ABO blood types.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: Which ecological pyramid is ALWAYS upright and can never be inverted in any ecosystem?

options.A: Pyramid of Energy
options.B: Pyramid of Biomass
options.C: Pyramid of Numbers
options.D: All pyramids can be inverted

questions.explanation: Pyramid of energy is always upright because energy is lost as heat at each trophic level (10% law of energy transfer), so energy at higher trophic levels is always less than lower levels.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Which of the following blood vessels carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs?

options.A: Pulmonary Artery
options.B: Pulmonary Vein
options.C: Aorta
options.D: Coronary Sinus

questions.explanation: The pulmonary artery arises from the right ventricle and carries deoxygenated blood to the lungs for oxygenation.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: The deoxygenated blood pumped into the pulmonary artery is passed on to the lungs from where the oxygenated blood is carried by the pulmonary veins into the left atrium.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: In ECG (Electrocardiogram), what does the T-wave represent?

options.A: Ventricular repolarisation
options.B: Ventricular depolarisation
options.C: Atrial depolarisation
options.D: Atrial repolarisation

questions.explanation: P-wave represents atrial depolarisation; QRS complex represents ventricular depolarisation; T-wave represents return of ventricles from excited to normal state (ventricular repolarisation).

ncert_reference.exact_quote: The T-wave represents the return of the ventricles from excited to normal state (repolarisation).

questions.question: The part of the human nephron that is impermeable to water but allows active reabsorption of electrolytes is:

options.B: Descending limb of Henle's loop
options.C: Proximal Convoluted Tubule (PCT)

questions.question: The Juxtaglomerular apparatus (JGA) releases renin in response to:

options.B: Rise in blood pressure

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Which of the following structures is NOT a part of nephron?

options.A: Collecting duct
options.B: Bowman's capsule
options.C: Glomerulus
options.D: Loop of Henle

questions.explanation: Each nephron consists of two parts: the glomerulus and the renal tubule (Bowman's capsule, PCT, Henle's loop, DCT). Multiple nephrons empty into a single collecting duct, so collecting duct is not strictly part of a single nephron.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: The collecting duct extends from the cortex of the kidney to the inner parts of the medulla. It is not considered an anatomical part of the nephron unit itself.

questions.question: The hormone calcitonin (thyrocalcitonin or TCT) is secreted by thyroid gland and acts to:

options.B: Increase blood calcium level (hypercalcemic)
options.C: Stimulate bone resorption

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: In the human male reproductive system, the scrotum helps in maintaining the low temperature of the testes necessary for spermatogenesis. How much below normal internal body temperature is this?

options.A: 2 - 2.5 °C lower than internal body temperature
options.B: 5 - 6 °C lower than internal body temperature
options.C: 0.5 - 1 °C lower than internal body temperature
options.D: 3.5 - 4 °C higher than internal body temperature

questions.explanation: The scrotum maintains the temperature of the testes 2-2.5 °C lower than the normal internal body temperature, which is essential for spermatogenesis.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: The scrotum helps in maintaining the low temperature of the testes (2–2.5 oC lower than the normal internal body temperature) necessary for spermatogenesis.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Which cells in the human testes provide nutrition to the developing germ cells (spermatogonia)?

options.A: Sertoli cells (Sustentacular cells)
options.B: Leydig cells (Interstitial cells)
options.C: Follicular cells
options.D: Chromaffin cells

questions.explanation: Each seminiferous tubule is lined on its inside by two types of cells: male germ cells (spermatogonia) and Sertoli cells. Sertoli cells provide nutrition to the developing germ cells.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Sertoli cells provide nutrition to the germ cells.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Leydig cells (interstitial cells) are present in the interstitial spaces between seminiferous tubules. What is their primary endocrine secretion?

options.A: Androgens (mainly Testosterone)
options.B: Inhibin and Relaxin
options.C: Luteinizing Hormone (LH)
options.D: Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH)

questions.explanation: Leydig cells synthesize and secrete testicular hormones called androgens (primarily testosterone) under the stimulation of LH from the anterior pituitary.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Leydig cells synthesise and secrete testicular hormones called androgens.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Which of the following represents the correct sequence of transport of sperm cells through the male accessory ducts?

options.A: Rete testis -> Vasa efferentia -> Epididymis -> Vas deferens
options.B: Rete testis -> Vas deferens -> Epididymis -> Vasa efferentia
options.C: Epididymis -> Rete testis -> Vasa efferentia -> Vas deferens
options.D: Vasa efferentia -> Rete testis -> Vas deferens -> Epididymis

questions.explanation: Seminiferous tubules open into rete testis, which leads via vasa efferentia to the epididymis located along the posterior surface of each testis, and then ascends as vas deferens.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: The seminiferous tubules of the testis open into the vasa efferentia through rete testis. The vasa efferentia leave the testis and open into epididymis... which leads to vas deferens.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Secretions of which male accessory glands are rich in fructose, calcium, and certain enzymes?

options.A: Seminal vesicles
options.B: Bulbourethral glands only
options.C: Prostate gland only
options.D: Bartholin glands

questions.explanation: The secretions of male accessory glands (paired seminal vesicles, a prostate, and paired bulbourethral glands) constitute the seminal plasma, which is rich in fructose, calcium and certain enzymes.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: The seminal plasma which is rich in fructose, calcium and certain enzymes. The secretions of bulbourethral glands also help in the lubrication of the penis.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: In the human female reproductive system, fertilization of the ovum normally takes place in which region of the fallopian tube (oviduct)?

options.A: Ampullary region (Ampulla)
options.B: Isthmus only
options.C: Infundibulum
options.D: Uterine fundus

questions.explanation: Fertilization takes place in the ampullary region of the fallopian tube where the sperm and ovum meet.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Fertilisation can only occur if the ovum and sperms are transported simultaneously to the ampullary region.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The finger-like projections at the edges of the infundibulum that help in collection of the ovum after ovulation are called:

options.A: Fimbriae
options.B: Ampullae
options.C: Mesovarium
options.D: Cilia

questions.explanation: The edges of the infundibulum possess finger-like projections called fimbriae, which help in collection of the ovum after ovulation.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: The edges of the infundibulum possess finger-like projections called fimbriae, which help in collection of the ovum after ovulation.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The wall of the uterus consists of three layers of tissue. Which middle thick layer of smooth muscle exhibits strong contractions during delivery of the baby?

options.A: Myometrium
options.B: Endometrium
options.C: Perimetrium
options.D: Epimetrium

questions.explanation: The middle thick layer of smooth muscle is the myometrium. The myometrium exhibits strong contraction during delivery of the baby.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Myometrium exhibits strong contraction during delivery of the baby.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Spermatogenesis begins at puberty due to a significant increase in the secretion of which hypothalamic hormone?

options.A: Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone (GnRH)
options.B: Prolactin
options.C: Human Growth Hormone
options.D: Oxytocin

questions.explanation: Spermatogenesis starts at the age of puberty due to significant increase in the secretion of gonadotropin releasing hormone (GnRH), a hypothalamic hormone.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Spermatogenesis starts at the age of puberty due to significant increase in the secretion of gonadotropin releasing hormone (GnRH).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The cap-like structure covering the anterior portion of the sperm head containing hydrolytic enzymes to penetrate the ovum is called:

options.A: Acrosome
options.B: Centriole
options.C: Mitochondrial spiral (Nebenkern)
options.D: Corona radiata

questions.explanation: The acrosome is filled with enzymes (including hyaluronidase and acrosin) that help fertilisation of the ovum.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: The acrosome is filled with enzymes that help fertilisation of the ovum.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: In human females, primary oocytes are arrested at which specific meiotic stage from embryonic life until puberty?

options.A: Prophase I (Diplotene stage) of Meiosis I
options.B: Metaphase II of Meiosis II
options.C: Anaphase I of Meiosis I
options.D: Telophase II of Meiosis II

questions.explanation: Primary oocytes start division and enter into prophase-I of the meiotic division and get temporarily arrested at that stage (diplotene).

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Primary oocytes start division and enter into prophase-I of the meiotic division and get temporarily arrested at that stage.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Secondary oocyte is arrested at which stage of cell division when released from the Graafian follicle during ovulation?

options.A: Metaphase II of Meiosis II
options.B: Prophase I of Meiosis I
options.C: Anaphase II of Meiosis II
options.D: Telophase I of Meiosis I

questions.explanation: The secondary oocyte is released at Metaphase II. Its second meiotic division is completed only upon sperm entry (fertilization).

ncert_reference.exact_quote: The entry of sperm induces the completion of the meiotic division of the secondary oocyte.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: During which phase of the menstrual cycle does rapid surge of LH (LH surge) induce rupture of the Graafian follicle and release of the ovum?

options.A: Mid-cycle (about 14th day)
options.B: Menstrual phase (days 1 to 5)
options.C: Secretory phase (days 21 to 28)
options.D: Follicular phase (day 5)

questions.explanation: Rapid secretion of LH leading to its maximum level during the mid-cycle called LH surge induces rupture of Graafian follicle and thereby the release of an ovum (ovulation).

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Rapid secretion of LH leading to its maximum level during the mid-cycle called LH surge induces rupture of Graafian follicle and thereby the release of an ovum (ovulation).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: After ovulation, the ruptured Graafian follicle transforms into a yellow endocrine structure called corpus luteum, which secretes large amounts of:

options.A: Progesterone
options.B: Estrogen only
options.C: FSH
options.D: Oxytocin

questions.explanation: The corpus luteum secretes large amounts of progesterone which is essential for maintenance of the endometrium for implantation and pregnancy.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: The corpus luteum secretes large amounts of progesterone which is essential for maintenance of the endometrium.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The non-cellular transparent glycoprotein coat surrounding the secondary oocyte which induces the acrosome reaction upon sperm contact is:

options.A: Zona pellucida
options.B: Corona radiata
options.C: Theca interna
options.D: Perivitelline space

questions.explanation: The secondary oocyte forms a new membrane called zona pellucida surrounding it. The sperm comes in contact with the zona pellucida and induces changes that block entry of additional sperms.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: During fertilisation, a sperm comes in contact with the zona pellucida layer of the ovum and induces changes in the membrane that block the entry of additional sperms.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Cleavage divisions of the human zygote produce 2, 4, 8, 16 daughter cells called blastomeres. The embryo with 8 to 16 blastomeres is specifically called a:

options.A: Morula
options.B: Blastocyst
options.C: Gastrula
options.D: Trophoblast

questions.explanation: The mitotic division called cleavage starts as the zygote moves through the isthmus towards the uterus and forms 2, 4, 8, 16 daughter cells called blastomeres. The embryo with 8 to 16 blastomeres is called a morula.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: The embryo with 8 to 16 blastomeres is called a morula.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Implantation in humans involves the attachment of which embryonic stage to the uterine endometrium?

options.A: Blastocyst
options.B: Morula
options.C: Gastrula
options.D: Zygote

questions.explanation: The blastocyst becomes embedded in the endometrium of the uterus. This is called implantation and it leads to pregnancy.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: The blastocyst becomes embedded in the endometrium of the uterus. This is called implantation and it leads to pregnancy.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Which of the following hormones is produced in women ONLY during pregnancy and not secreted in non-pregnant states?

options.A: hCG, hPL and Relaxin
options.B: Estrogen and Progesterone
options.C: Oxytocin and Vasopressin
options.D: Thyroxine and Prolactin

questions.explanation: hCG (Human Chorionic Gonadotropin), hPL (Human Placental Lactogen) and relaxin (produced by the ovary in later pregnancy) are produced in women only during pregnancy.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: hCG, hPL and relaxin are produced in women only during pregnancy.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The fetal ejection reflex during human parturition originates from which source?

options.A: Fully developed fetus and the placenta
options.B: Maternal pituitary gland alone
options.C: Maternal adrenal cortex
options.D: Corpus luteum of ovary

questions.explanation: Parturition signals originate from the fully developed fetus and the placenta which induce mild uterine contractions called fetal ejection reflex, triggering release of oxytocin from maternal pituitary.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: The signals for parturition originate from the fully developed foetus and the placenta which induce mild uterine contractions called foetal ejection reflex.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Colostrum, the yellowish fluid secreted by the mother during initial days of lactation, contains abundant amounts of which protective antibody?

options.A: IgA
options.B: IgG
options.C: IgM
options.D: IgE

questions.explanation: Colostrum contains abundant antibodies (primarily IgA) to provide passive immunity and protect the newborn infant against various infectious pathogens.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: What is the ploidy level of primary spermatocytes, secondary spermatocytes, and spermatids respectively?

options.A: 2n, n, n
options.B: n, n, n
options.C: 2n, 2n, n
options.D: 2n, n, 2n

questions.explanation: Primary spermatocytes are diploid (2n, 46 chromosomes). After Meiosis I, secondary spermatocytes are haploid (n, 23 chromosomes). After Meiosis II, spermatids are haploid (n, 23 chromosomes).

ncert_reference.exact_quote: A primary spermatocyte completes the first meiotic division leading to formation of two equal, haploid cells called secondary spermatocytes (23 chromosomes each).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The process of transformation of non-motile spermatids into functional mature spermatozoa is termed:

options.A: Spermiogenesis
options.B: Spermiation
options.C: Spermatocytogenesis
options.D: Insemination

questions.explanation: The spermatids are transformed into spermatozoa (sperms) by the process called spermiogenesis. After spermiogenesis, sperm heads become embedded in the Sertoli cells and are finally released by spermiation.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: The spermatids are transformed into spermatozoa (sperms) by the process called spermiogenesis.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Spermiation refers to which specific event in the male reproductive tract?

options.A: Release of mature sperms from the Sertoli cells into the cavity of seminiferous tubules
options.B: Transformation of spermatid to spermatozoon
options.C: Discharge of semen into the female vagina
options.D: Ejaculation of semen from the male penis

questions.explanation: After spermiogenesis, sperm heads become embedded in the Sertoli cells, and are finally released from the seminiferous tubules by the process called spermiation.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: After spermiogenesis, sperm heads become embedded in the Sertoli cells, and are finally released from the seminiferous tubules by the process called spermiation.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: For normal male fertility, what percentage of the total ejaculated sperms must possess normal shape and size, and what percentage of those must show vigorous motility?

options.A: At least 60% normal shape and size, and at least 40% vigorous motility
options.B: At least 40% normal shape, and at least 60% vigorous motility
options.C: 50% normal shape, and 50% vigorous motility
options.D: 75% normal shape, and 25% vigorous motility

questions.explanation: For normal fertility, at least 60 per cent of sperms must have normal shape and size and at least 40 per cent of them must show vigorous motility.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: For normal fertility, at least 60 per cent sperms must have normal shape and size and at least 40 per cent of them must show vigorous motility.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: By the end of which gestational month are the limbs and digits fully formed in a developing human embryo?

options.A: End of the second month (8 weeks)
options.B: End of the first month (4 weeks)
options.C: End of the third month (12 weeks)
options.D: End of the fifth month (20 weeks)

questions.explanation: By the end of the second month of pregnancy, the foetus develops limbs and digits. By the end of 12 weeks (first trimester), most of the major organ systems are formed.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: By the end of the second month of pregnancy, the foetus develops limbs and digits.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: First movements of the fetus and appearance of hair on its head are usually observed during which month of pregnancy?

options.A: Fifth month
options.B: Third month
options.C: Sixth month
options.D: Seventh month

questions.explanation: The first movements of the foetus and appearance of hair on the head are usually observed during the fifth month of gestation.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: The first movements of the foetus and appearance of hair on the head are usually observed during the fifth month.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Which hormone acts on the uterine muscle (myometrium) and causes stronger and stronger contractions during labor?

options.A: Oxytocin
options.B: Progesterone
options.C: Prolactin
options.D: Vasopressin

questions.explanation: Oxytocin released from the maternal posterior pituitary acts on the uterine muscle and causes stronger uterine contractions, which in turn stimulates further secretion of oxytocin (positive feedback loop).

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Oxytocin acts on the uterine muscle and causes stronger uterine contractions, which in turn stimulates further secretion of oxytocin.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The structural and functional unit between the developing embryo (foetus) and maternal body is called:

options.A: Placenta
options.B: Amnion
options.C: Chorion alone
options.D: Allantois

questions.explanation: The chorionic villi and uterine tissue become interdigitated with each other and jointly form a structural and functional unit between developing embryo (foetus) and maternal body called placenta.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: The chorionic villi and uterine tissue become interdigitated with each other and jointly form a structural and functional unit between developing embryo (foetus) and maternal body called placenta.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: The inner cell mass of the blastocyst contains certain cells that have the potency to give rise to all tissues and organs. These cells are called:

options.A: Stem cells
options.B: Trophoblasts
options.C: Blastoderm cells
options.D: Mesenchymal cells

questions.explanation: The inner cell mass contains certain cells called stem cells which have the potency to give rise to all the tissues and organs of the adult organism.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: The inner cell mass contains certain cells called stem cells which have the potency to give rise to all the tissues and organs.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: During oogenesis, the second meiotic division results in the formation of:

options.A: A haploid ovum (ootid) and a second polar body
options.B: Two equal diploid ova
options.C: Primary oocyte and first polar body
options.D: Four equal functional ova

questions.explanation: The second meiotic division is unequal and results in the formation of a second polar body and a haploid ovum (ootid).

ncert_reference.exact_quote: The second meiotic division is also unequal and results in the formation of a second polar body and a haploid ovum (ootid).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Which of the following hormones is NOT secreted by human placenta during pregnancy?

options.A: Luteinizing Hormone (LH)
options.B: Human Chorionic Gonadotropin (hCG)
options.C: Human Placental Lactogen (hPL)
options.D: Estrogens and Progesterones

questions.explanation: Placenta produces hormones like hCG, hPL, estrogens, progesterone and relaxin (in later phase). LH (Luteinizing Hormone) is secreted by the anterior pituitary gland, not the placenta.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Placenta also acts as an endocrine tissue and produces several hormones like human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG), human placental lactogen (hPL), estrogens, progestogens, etc.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: In human males, the Leydig cells (interstitial cells) are present in the interstitial spaces of testes and secrete:

options.A: Androgens (Testosterone)
options.B: Inhibin
options.C: Estrogen
options.D: Prolactin

questions.explanation: Leydig cells synthesize and secrete testicular hormones called androgens (chiefly testosterone).

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Leydig cells synthesise and secrete testicular hormones called androgens.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Which of the following hormones is responsible for triggering ovulation and maintenance of corpus luteum in the human menstrual cycle?

options.A: Luteinizing Hormone (LH)
options.B: Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH)
options.C: Prolactin
options.D: Oxytocin

questions.explanation: Rapid secretion of LH leading to its maximum level during the mid-cycle called LH surge induces rupture of Graafian follicle and thereby release of ovum (ovulation). LH also maintains the corpus luteum.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Rapid secretion of LH leading to its maximum level during the mid-cycle called LH surge induces rupture of Graafian follicle and thereby the release of an ovum (ovulation).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Which of the following is an intrauterine device (IUD) that releases copper ions (Cu2+) to suppress sperm motility?

options.A: CuT and Multiload 375
options.B: Lippes loop
options.C: Progestasert
options.D: LNG-20

questions.explanation: Copper releasing IUDs (CuT, Cu7, Multiload 375) release Cu ions which suppress sperm motility and the fertilising capacity of sperms.

ncert_reference.official_section: Section 4.2: Population Explosion and Birth Control
ncert_reference.exact_quote: Cu ions released suppress sperm motility and the fertilising capacity of sperms.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Which of the following sexually transmitted infections (STIs) is caused by the bacterium Treponema pallidum?

options.A: Syphilis
options.B: Gonorrhoea
options.C: Genital herpes
options.D: Trichomoniasis

questions.explanation: Syphilis is caused by Treponema pallidum. Gonorrhoea is caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Genital herpes is caused by Herpes simplex virus.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Syphilis, gonorrhoea, genital herpes, chlamydiasis, genital warts, trichomoniasis are examples of sexually transmitted infections.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: In the Hardy-Weinberg equation p^2 + 2pq + q^2 = 1, what does the term 2pq represent?

options.A: Frequency of heterozygous individuals (Aa)
options.B: Frequency of homozygous dominant individuals (AA)
options.C: Frequency of homozygous recessive individuals (aa)
options.D: Frequency of dominant allele

questions.explanation: In a diploid population, p^2 represents the frequency of homozygous dominant (AA), q^2 represents homozygous recessive (aa), and 2pq represents heterozygous individuals (Aa).

ncert_reference.exact_quote: Individual frequencies can be named p and q... The frequency of individuals with Aa is 2pq.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a secondary lymphoid organ where mature lymphocytes interact with antigens?

options.A: Spleen and Lymph nodes
options.B: Bone marrow
options.C: Thymus
options.D: Thyroid

questions.explanation: Primary lymphoid organs are bone marrow and thymus where immature lymphocytes differentiate. Secondary lymphoid organs include spleen, lymph nodes, tonsils, Peyer's patches, where lymphocytes encounter antigens.

ncert_reference.exact_quote: The secondary lymphoid organs are spleen, lymph nodes, tonsils, Peyer's patches of small intestine and appendix.
